claim: Attacking a Pokémon's Weakness type adds a bonus on top of base attack damage, shown as a discrete 'Weakness 100' indicator for Ho-Oh ex's Phoenix Turbo vs. Varoom, taking the 70-HP target to 0 HP (instant KO).

result.evidence: Ho-Oh ex (Fire, A4 034) Phoenix Turbo 80 into Varoom (70 HP, weak Fire). The attack goes through active_damage_effect_doutcome (apply_attack_action.rs:426-428, 2351-2370) and then modify_damage. printed_weakness_application returns Flat(20) when the defender's Weakness is one of the attacker's types (hooks/core.rs:1486-1513, Flat(20) at 1509), and it only applies Active-to-Active (core.rs:1455-1466). after_weakness = pre_weakness + 20 (core.rs:1876-1880), so 80 + 20 = 100, which is at least 70 and gives a KO. Tests: ho_oh_ex_phoenix_turbo_test.rs:35-45 pins the base 80 against a non-weak Chansey; core.rs:2851-2862 (weakness_adds_20_when_weak_and_nothing_when_not) pins the +20.
result.note: The engine has no on-screen 'Weakness 100' indicator, only the arithmetic, which matches. rules/02_damage_knockouts_points.md:28 already records this observation.

claim: Weakness adds a flat +20 to attack damage rather than doubling it, confirmed repeatedly: Electro Ball 40→60, Netherwing 130→150, and three further hits of 90→110, 120→140, 60→80 across separate matches.

result.evidence: Weakness is WeaknessApplication::Flat(20) (hooks/core.rs:1509), added once after attacker boosts (core.rs:1876-1880). It becomes x2 only while Bounded Field is in play and the attacker is not a Mega ex (core.rs:1502-1508). Tests: core.rs:2851-2862 (Mewtwo ex 50 into Riolu = 70); observed_gameplay_outcomes_test.rs:258-321 (Celebi ex 100 raw + 20 Grass Weakness = 120 into Rampardos); stadium_test.rs:887-930 (comment and assert: normal Weakness is 30+20, x2 only under Bounded Field).
result.note: The engine database card types are consistent with the claimed examples: Electro Ball 40 (Team Rocket's Zapdos ex, Lightning) becomes 60, and Netherwing 130 (Team Rocket's Moltres ex, Fire) becomes 150. The engine gives +20 on any such hit when no Bounded Field is in play.

claim: Flat damage bonuses from abilities/attack effects stack additively with Weakness's flat +20: Happiny's Chubby Cheer +20 plus Weakness +20 made a 10-base attack hit for 50; Falinks's Invade(20)+Coordinated Unit(+20)+Weakness(+20)=60, KOing a 50-HP Eevee.

result.evidence: All attacker-side boosts are summed into pre_weakness, then the flat +20 is added (hooks/core.rs:1854-1861, 1876-1880). Chubby Cheer's exact text maps to Mechanic::IncreasedDamageNextTurn{20, energy_type: None} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2523-2528). That mechanic stores TurnEffect::IncreasedDamageForPlayer with duration 2 (apply_attack_action.rs:1641-1656), and it counts for any of that player's Active-to-Active attacks (core.rs:1045-1054). So 10 + 20 + 20 = 50. Falinks's Coordinated Unit offensive +20 is added when another Falinks is in play (core.rs:1012-1024), so Invade 20 + 20 + Weakness 20 = 60, which KOs a 50-HP Eevee (weak Fighting). Tests: inspiring_dance_test.rs:21-50 uses Oricorio, whose attack text is identical and maps to the same mechanic, and pins 10 becoming 30 on the next turn. falinks_coordinated_unit_test.rs:50-60 pins Invade 20 + 20 = 40.
result.note: No single test pins a boost together with Weakness. Their sum rests on the additive code at core.rs:1854-1880. Happiny itself is Colorless, so the Weakness hit must have come from a different attacker, and the engine gives the +20 to any of that player's attackers.

claim: The Bounded Field Stadium changes the Weakness modifier from a flat bonus to a x2 multiplier on base damage, shown by 60x2-50=70.

result.evidence: Under Bounded Field, printed_weakness_application returns Double for attackers that are not Mega ex (hooks/core.rs:1502-1508). after_weakness = pre_weakness * 2 (core.rs:1879), and defender reductions are subtracted after that (core.rs:1883-1885). Test rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:173-202 reproduces this exact case, 60 Fire (Ninetales) into Skarmory ex holding Metal Core Barrier under Bounded Field, and asserts 70 (line 199). stadium_test.rs:887-930 pins 30 becoming 60.
result.note: One nuance: the engine doubles the pre-Weakness total, which is base plus attacker boosts minus attacker debuffs, not only the printed base. stadium_test.rs:963-1003 pins (20 + Red 20) x2 = 80, and rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:204-231 pins (60 - Intimidating Fang 20) x2 = 80. Mega ex attackers keep +20. The observed 60x2-50 case had no attacker modifiers, so it cannot tell 'base' apart from 'pre-Weakness total'.

claim: Damage-reduction effects (Tools/Supporters/Abilities) from different sources stack additively on one attack and floor the total at exactly 0, never negative: Falinks's -20 cut 10 to 0; Steel Wing's -20 cut 70 to 50 (0 combined with Metal Core Barrier); Jasmine+Steel Wing cut 130 to 60 and 70 to 0.

result.evidence: Defender reductions from different sources are collected in FiniteDamageReductions: heavy_helmet, metal_core_barrier, steel_apron, ability, conditional_ability, coordinated_unit, card_effect and turn_effect (hooks/core.rs:1276-1307, 1330-1378). They are summed (total_u64) and subtracted once with saturating_sub, so the result floors at 0 (core.rs:1883-1885). The pieces: Steel Wing is CardEffect::ReducedDamage{20} with duration 1 (effect_mechanic_map.rs:603-610; counted at core.rs:1147-1167). Jasmine is TurnEffect::ReducedDamageForTarget{50, NamedPokemon[Steelix, Skarmory ex]} (apply_trainer_action.rs:1021-1037, 1056-1059; counted at core.rs:1189-1227). Metal Core Barrier -50 is at core.rs:715-735, Steel Apron -10 at core.rs:737-762, and the Coordinated Unit defensive -20 at core.rs:912-937. So 70-20 = 50, 70-20-50 = 0, 130-50-20 = 60, 70-70 = 0 and 10-20 floors at 0. Tests for the floor: rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:200 (10+20-50 gives 0), core.rs:2864-2869 (Solid Shell 20-20 = 0), damage_reduction_trainers_test.rs:113-129 (Jasmine -50 fully absorbs 30). Test for Coordinated Unit -20: falinks_coordinated_unit_test.rs:69-79.
result.note: No test combines two different reduction sources on one hit (Steel Wing with Metal Core Barrier, or Jasmine with Steel Wing). Their stacking rests on the summing code. Steel Wing's stored reduction only counts for Active-to-Active hits (core.rs:1153-1155), which fits all of the listed cases.

claim: A defending Pokemon's own attached Energy count appears to scale the attacker's damage upward: 120 damage matched a base of 30 plus 30 per Energy on a defender holding 3 Energy.

result.evidence: Indeedee ex's Psychic text ('30 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon') maps to Mechanic::ExtraDamagePerEnergy{opponent: true, damage_per_energy: 30, include_fixed_damage: true} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2204-2211). That is evaluated by extra_damage_per_energy, which computes base + (number of Energy on the opponent's Active) x 30 (apply_attack_action.rs:872-885, 4363-4381). So 30 + 3x30 = 120. Indeedee ex is Psychic and Articuno / Team Rocket's Articuno ex are weak to Lightning / Metal, so no Weakness is added. The same mechanic is pinned for Exeggutor's Psychic by observed_gameplay_outcomes_test.rs:114-161 (80 + 20 for 1 Energy + 20 Weakness = 120) and :163-182 (0 Energy gives 80).
result.note: The claim is marked 'inferred', but it simply restates Indeedee ex's printed text, and the engine implements that text exactly. No test pins Indeedee ex specifically. rules/02 line 26 also lists Indeedee ex's observed damage of 90, 120 and 180.

claim: When Weakness and a flat Tool damage reduction both apply, Weakness's +20 is added to base damage before the flat reduction is subtracted (200+20-10=210).

result.evidence: modify_damage adds Weakness first (hooks/core.rs:1876-1880), then subtracts defender reductions including Steel Apron (core.rs:1883-1885; steel_apron_reduction at 737-762, -10 on a Metal holder hit by the opponent). Charizard ex Crimson Storm 200 (Fire) into Skarmory ex (Metal, weak Fire) with Steel Apron gives 200 + 20 - 10 = 210. The Weakness-before-reduction order is pinned by rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:173-202, where 10 + 20 - 50 gives 0 (line 200) and not the reversed-order 20. steel_apron_test.rs:160-187 pins the -10.
result.note: The 200+20-10 example does not by itself test the order: with no floor, subtracting first also gives 210. The engine's order agrees with the claim anyway.

claim: Aegislash's Superb Shield reduces damage by 80 only from the opponent's Pokémon ex attacks during the opponent's next turn (reduction, not immunity); non-ex attacks and Ability damage land at full value.

result.evidence: Superb Shield's text maps to DamageAndCardEffect{CardEffect::ReducedDamageFromEx{80}, duration: 1} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2554-2562). Duration 1 means 'during opponent's next turn' (state/played_card.rs:340-346, 460-468). The reduction counts only when attacker_is_ex and only for Active-to-Active attacks (hooks/core.rs:1147-1167, line 1163). It is a finite reduction with saturating_sub, not a prevention (core.rs:1883-1885). Crobat's Cunning Link applies its 30 through handle_damage with is_from_active_attack = false (apply_abilities_action.rs:69-71, 737-751). That makes is_active_to_active false (core.rs:1737), so the reduction is 0 and the full 30 lands. Tests: aegislash_superb_shield_test.rs:33-60 (Mega Latios ex 160 cut to 80) and :62-89 (non-ex Melmetal does its full 120).
result.note: Crobat's Darkness Fang (50, not an ex) also lands in full. Crobat isn't an ex, so the Cunning Link case would be unreduced even if Ability damage were treated as attack damage (rules/02 line 79 says the same).

claim: Multiple damage instances within a turn subtract directly from current HP with no reduction applied, confirmed across a 5-step chain (210→180→160→90→50) and a separate case (130→10 from 120 damage).

result.evidence: Each damage instance adds to damage_counters with no per-turn cap (state/played_card.rs:231-233, apply_damage). Attack damage goes through handle_damage_only and is then applied to HP (actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:518-590, apply at 565-570). Rocky Helmet-style retaliation is applied directly with attacker.apply_damage and no modifiers (apply_action_helpers.rs:593-605). On-KO Ability damage (Destiny Burst) is built at hooks/core.rs:2200-2220. Ability and retaliation damage is never reduced by 'from attacks' reductions (they gate on is_from_active_attack, e.g. core.rs:720, 743, 1153). The 130 to 10 case is Team Rocket's Articuno ex (130 HP) taking 120, the same hit as R6.
result.note: The support is weak: both sources say 'unspecified', and the board state at each step isn't given. The engine would apply any attack reduction that was in play, so 'no reduction applied' only holds if none was. rules/_research_notes/R2_battle_observations.md:218 identifies part of the 225430 chain: Rocky Helmet takes 180 to 160, then Destiny Burst takes 160 to 90. Both land raw in the engine. tests/pokemon/team_rocket_electrode_destiny_burst_test.rs:8-63 covers that sequence (points and KOs only, no HP values).

claim: An effect gave a Pokémon a marker after the notice 'Prevent damage from attacks if heads is flipped,' but the coin flip's actual result was unreadable, so whether damage prevention triggered is unconfirmed.

result.evidence: The card is Meowth B2 124/204, whose Ability Carefree Steps reads 'If any damage is done to this Pokémon by attacks, flip a coin. If heads, prevent that damage.' In the engine it is a passive Ability that presents as CardEffect::CoinFlipToPreventIncomingDamage (effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:1003-1005). At attack resolution the outcome splits into heads and tails for each Meowth that takes damage (apply_attack_action.rs:184-216). Tests: meowth_carefree_steps_test.rs:19-65 (heads prevents only the damage and the Poison still lands) and :74-152 (independent flips per Benched Meowth).
result.note: The claim asserts no outcome: the coin was unreadable, and it is marked 'unclear'. In the engine this is a permanent Ability, not a 'marker' added by an effect. To settle it, find a frame where the coin face is readable, plus Meowth's HP before and after that hit. Heads should mean no HP change from the attack's damage, with the attack's other effects still applied.

claim: Ho-Oh ex's Phoenix Turbo attaches 1 Fire + 1 Water + 1 Lightning Energy to a Benched Pokémon on the attacker's own side each use; the targeted Benched Pokémon can vary between uses.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:28706, A4 034): 80 damage, 'Take a [R], [W], and [L] Energy from your Energy Zone and attach them to your Benched Basic Pokémon in any way you like.' Engine maps it at engine/src/actions/effect_mechanic_map.rs:1840-1845 to AttachEnergiesAnyWayToBenchedBasic{Fire,Water,Lightning}, dispatched at apply_attack_action.rs:426-427. The body is apply_attack_action.rs:2351-2393: damage first, then one Attach choice for each way of placing each Energy on a Benched Basic, so all three on one Pokémon is offered, and the choice is made fresh on every use. Pinned by engine/tests/pokemon/ho_oh_ex_phoenix_turbo_test.rs:18-93: 80 damage, 8 distributions across 2 Basics, all-on-one Bulbasaur accepted, a split also offered. Lines 95-133 cover a Fossil target and lines 135-172 the fizzle when no Basic is benched.
result.note: The engine only allows Benched Basic Pokémon, which is what the card says. The claim says 'a Benched Pokémon'. It only conflicts if the video showed Energy going onto an evolved Benched Pokémon; the recorded evidence does not say that.

claim: Lugia ex's Elemental Blast deals 180 damage and, after damage resolves, discards 1 Fire + 1 Water + 1 Lightning Energy from Lugia as its cost/effect.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:31381-31384, A4 149): [R][W][L], 180, 'Discard a [R], [W], and [L] Energy from this Pokémon.' Engine maps it at effect_mechanic_map.rs:219-224 to SelfDiscardEnergy{Fire,Water,Lightning}, dispatched at apply_attack_action.rs:625-627 to self_energy_discard_attack (2888-2892). That function is active_damage_effect_doutcome(180, discard...), so the discard runs as the post-damage effect. The ordering is set by attack_outcome.rs:67-77 (damage_then_effect) and 134-209, which runs the pre-effect, then damage, then the post-effect (line 180), then retaliation, then knockouts. The discard takes exactly one of each named type (apply_attack_action.rs:2858-2885).
result.note: No Lugia-specific test exists, so this rests on code reading only. The ordering path is the same one the Gouging Fire and Walking Wake tests exercise.

claim: An attack cannot be used unless its full Energy cost is attached: Cold Start requires 2 Water + 1 Colorless, and with only 2 Water attached at turn's end, Iron Bundle ex could not use it that turn.

result.evidence: The engine only offers an attack when its cost can be paid: engine/src/move_generation/attacks.rs:70-76 calls contains_energy(active, modified_cost). hooks/core.rs:2099-2135 (energy_missing) matches typed Energy first, then counts what is left against Colorless. With W,W attached against W,W,C, zero Energy is left for the Colorless, so one Colorless is missing and Cold Start is not offered. The engine's cost is the same (database.rs:69501: [Water, Water, Colorless]). The missing-Energy case is pinned by the unit test hooks/core.rs:2524-2532 (test_contains_energy_false_missing).
result.note: There is no Iron Bundle-specific 'can't attack' test. The core.rs test covers the general check. Cost changes through get_attack_cost could alter this, but none apply to the case described.

claim: Primarina ex's Sparkling Aria both deals 100 damage to the opponent's Active and heals the user 20 HP as part of the same attack, shown as a 90→110 HP self-heal alongside the opposing KO.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:26003-26005): [W][W][W], 100, 'Heal 20 damage from this Pokémon.' Engine maps it at effect_mechanic_map.rs:1150-1151 to SelfHeal{20}, dispatched at apply_attack_action.rs:356 to self_heal_attack (3361-3365). That function is active_damage_effect_doutcome(100, heal_pokemon(actor, 0, 20)), so the heal is part of the same attack. The heal still happens on a KO: in attack_outcome.rs:134-209 the post-damage effect runs at line 180, before handle_knockouts at line 208. heal_pokemon (state/mod.rs:863-873) heals min(20, damage counters), so 90 goes to 110 while the defender is knocked out.
result.note: No Primarina test exists. A similar 'heals even when it knocks out' case is pinned for another card at engine/tests/pokemon/kabutops_leech_life_test.rs:77-94.

claim: Hau adds a flat +30 damage to the Supporter-player's attack that same turn; applied twice here, turning an 80-damage Hydro Pump into 110 and a 100-damage Sparkling Aria into 130.

result.evidence: Hau (lib/deckgym-database.json:27004): 'During this turn, attacks used by your Decidueye ex, Incineroar ex, or Primarina ex do +30 damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon.' Engine: apply_trainer_action.rs:275 sends Hau to hau_effect (1003-1016), which adds TurnEffect::IncreasedDamageForSpecificPokemon{30, [Decidueye ex, Incineroar ex, Primarina ex]} with duration 0. add_turn_effect (state/mod.rs:1063-1069) stores duration 0 for the current turn only. hooks/core.rs:1069-1087 adds +30 when the attacker's name matches and the attack is Active-to-Active. Hydro Pump is 40 +40 with an extra [W] (effect_mechanic_map.rs:1309-1313), so 80+30=110. Sparkling Aria is 100+30=130.
result.note: The claim says 'the Supporter-player's attack' in general. The engine, like the card, applies it only to Decidueye ex, Incineroar ex and Primarina ex; both observed attacks were Primarina ex's, so they fit. No Hau test exists; this is from code reading.

claim: Gallade ex's Energized Blade deals 70 base +20 damage per Energy attached to the OPPONENT's Active Pokémon (not the user's own Energy); confirmed twice at 70+20×1=90 while the defending Mega Blaziken held exactly 1 Fire Energy.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:10646-10648): 70, 'This attack does 20 more damage for each Energy attached to your opponent's Active Pokémon.' Engine maps it at effect_mechanic_map.rs:2105-2110 to ExtraDamagePerEnergy{opponent:true, 20, include_fixed_damage:true}. Dispatch is at apply_attack_action.rs:872-885 and extra_damage_per_energy (4363-4381) counts Energy on the opponent's Active. Pinned by engine/tests/pokemon/gallade_test.rs:13-47: Gallade holds 2 Energy and the defender holds 3, and the result is 130 (70+20×3), not 110, so it reads the opponent's Energy. Lines 49-77 pin the 0-Energy case at 70. With 1 Fire on Mega Blaziken the engine gives 90 (no Weakness applies: Fighting against a Water Weakness).

claim: Mega Blaziken ex's Mega Burning deals 120 damage, applies Burn to the opponent's Active, and discards 1 of its own attached Fire Energy after the attack resolves, confirmed consistently across many separate uses.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:44960-44963, B1 036): [R][R], 120, 'Discard Fire[R] Energy from this Pokémon. Your opponent's Active Pokémon is now Burned.' Engine maps it at effect_mechanic_map.rs:183-188 to SelfDiscardEnergyAndInflictStatus{[Fire], [Burned]}, dispatched at apply_attack_action.rs:628-635 to self_discard_energy_and_inflict_status (2894-2907). That function deals 120, then as the post-damage effect discards exactly one Fire (2858-2885) and applies Burn. attack_outcome.rs:180-209 runs this after damage and before retaliation and knockouts, which matches the order in rules/02_damage_knockouts_points.md:97-98 (Burn and discard still happen on a lethal hit).
result.note: No Mega Blaziken-specific test exists; this is from code reading. The engine discards the Fire before applying Burn inside the same post-damage step. The claim does not order those two, so there is nothing to conflict.

claim: Dewott's Razor Shell requires a coin flip to resolve; on Tails the attack deals 0 damage, a full miss rather than a partial reduction, confirmed on separate uses.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:75842-75845, B4 043 Dewott): [W], 20, 'Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 30 more damage.' Engine: effect_mechanic_map.rs:1018-1019 maps it to CoinFlipExtraDamage{30}. apply_attack_action.rs:581-583 sends it to coinflip_extra_damage_attack (1891-1896), which is binary_coin(active_damage_outcome(base+30), active_damage_outcome(base)). The engine's base is 20 (database.rs:74875-74879), so on tails the engine deals 20, not 0. The engine agrees with the printed card; the claim does not.
result.note: This is not an 'if tails, this attack does nothing' card, so a 0 on tails would need something else, such as damage reduction or prevention on the defender that turn, or a misread attack or number. To settle it, re-check the frames at about 2:32-2:55 of ScreenRecording_08-26-2026 21-47-38_1 for the defender and any active effects. If a bare Razor Shell on tails really shows 0 with nothing reducing it, the engine's tails branch (1894) is wrong.

claim: Scorching Interruption (Gouging Fire) requires discarding 2 Energy of the player's choice after the attack, and applies a -30 damage penalty to the opponent's very next attack regardless of which opposing Pokémon makes it (a nominal 40 became a shown 10).

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:71299-71302): [R][L][C], 100, 'Discard 2 Energy from this Pokémon. During your opponent's next turn, this Pokémon takes -30 damage from attacks.' Engine: effect_mechanic_map.rs:3388-3393 maps it to SelfDiscardChosenEnergyAndCardEffect{2, ReducedDamage{30}, 1}. apply_attack_action.rs:3704-3723 deals damage, then offers ChooseAttackEnergyDiscard options. apply_action.rs:834-844 discards the chosen Energy and adds ReducedDamage to Gouging Fire. hooks/core.rs:1147-1166 subtracts it from any Active-to-Active hit on that Pokémon, whoever the attacker is. Pinned by engine/tests/pokemon/energy_discard_combo_attacks_test.rs:169-233 (damage before the choice, player picks Lightning+Colorless, the opponent's 30 becomes 0 next turn). Also by engine/tests/rules_repair_energy_choice.rs:20-64 (the choice comes after damage and before retaliation and KO, and only distinct choices are offered).
result.note: The engine puts the -30 on Gouging Fire as damage it takes, as the card says, not on the attacker. It works 'regardless of which opposing Pokémon' attacks, but only while Gouging Fire is the Active being hit. The observed 40→10 fits either reading.

claim: Walking Wake's Sweeping Billow damages the Active target and also deals a flat 20 to every one of the opponent's Benched Pokémon (all of them, not a chosen subset), then requires discarding 1 Energy of the player's choice.

claim: Cynthia's damage-boost effect applies only to attacks made specifically by the player's own Garchomp or Togekiss; it had no effect the turn it was played here since neither of those attacked.

result.evidence: Cynthia (lib/deckgym-database.json:11871): 'During this turn, attacks used by your Garchomp or Togekiss do +50 damage to your opponent's Active Pokémon.' claim: Probopass's Triple Nose damage scales with heads flipped: observed as 130 for 2 heads/1 tail, 30 for 0 heads/3 tails, and 180 for 3 heads/0 tails.

claim: Heat Charged's coin-flip batch (e.g., 2 heads/1 tail) is shown before Victory Star offers an optional reflip; declining keeps the original batch, and Heat Charged then attaches Fire Energy matching the number of heads.

result.evidence: Test engine/tests/b4a_attack_batch2_test.rs:82-107 (victory_star_pauses_heat_charged_before_energy_and_keep_commits_once) covers this with Team Rocket's Moltres ex (B4a 007) and Victini. Victory Star is offered only when the Active is Fire-type and Victini's once-per-turn flag is unused (apply_action.rs:167-181). claim: Mega Sharpedo ex's Turbo Shark secondary effect (attach Energy to a Benched Water-type) still resolves after lethal primary damage and before KO/promotion processing; with no eligible target it does nothing, confirmed across multiple uses.

result.evidence: Turbo Shark text maps to ChargeBench{[W], target_benched_type: Water} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:3027-3032), which runs energy_bench_attack (apply_attack_action.rs:2318-2345). The engine maps it to BenchCountDamage{include_fixed_damage:true, damage_per:20, bench_side:YourBench} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2141-2148), and apply_attack_action.rs:2558-2595 computes 70 + 20 x (the attacker's own benched count). Unit test test_arceus_does_90_damage (apply_attack_action.rs:6877-6905) pins Arceus ex with 1 benched Pokémon at 90.
result.note: The claim only points to C5-18, which I could not find in the repo. This verdict covers the Ultimate Force mechanic as printed. If C5-18 says something else, check it against this code path.

claim: Happiny's Chubby Cheer gives +20 damage to the owner's next attack; the bonus persisted after Happiny was Knocked Out on the opponent's intervening turn and applied instead to a different attacker, producing 40 total damage.

result.evidence: Chubby Cheer (B4a 063/077) uses the same text as Oricorio's Inspiring Dance and maps to IncreasedDamageNextTurn{amount:20, energy_type:None} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2523-2527). apply_attack_action.rs:1641-1656 stores it as a player-level TurnEffect::IncreasedDamageForPlayer{player: actor} with duration 2 in state.turn_effects, keyed by turn number (state/mod.rs:1063-1078). The effect is not attached to Happiny, and nothing removes it when Happiny is Knocked Out: the only turn_effects removal is for ForceFirstHeads (state/mod.rs:1042-1053). hooks/core.rs:1045-1054 adds +20 to any attack by that player's Pokémon against the opponent's Active. So a different attacker, such as Absol's 20-damage Unseen Claw or Enhanced Blade, does 20+20=40. Test inspiring_dance_test.rs:22-50 pins the +20 two turns later and :55-81 pins that the opponent's attacks don't get it.
result.note: No test covers the exact case where the Chubby Cheer user is KO'd and a different Pokémon attacks. That part comes from reading the code: the bonus is player-scoped and isn't cleared by a KO. The bonus only applies to damage against the Active, so a bench attack like Absol's Leap Over would not get it.

claim: Mega Lucario ex's Fighting Pulse gets one flat +50 bonus if at least 1 more Energy is attached than the attack's cost; a 4th extra Fighting Energy attached did not add a second +50 increment.

result.evidence: Fighting Pulse (B3 081, lib/deckgym-database.json:66629-66632): 90, +50 "if this Pokémon has at least 1 extra [F] Energy attached." The engine maps it to ExtraDamageIfExtraEnergy{required_extra_energy:[Fighting], extra_damage:50} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:3290-3294). extra_energy_attack (apply_attack_action.rs:3254-3281) checks once whether the attacker holds the cost plus one more [F] and adds a single flat +50. It never counts further extras, so 4 or more [F] still gives 140. Tests lucario_b3_test.rs:99-126 (2 F = 90) and :129-161 (3 F = 140) pin the base and boosted values.
result.note: The extra Energy must be [F]. The claim says 'at least 1 more Energy' in general, but the observed extra was Fighting. No test checks 4+ Fighting Energy, but the code is a yes/no check.

claim: Tropical Swing requires a coin flip to deal damage; a Heads result lets it deal its full listed 80 damage, which KO'd 30-HP Bonsly.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:531-534, Exeggutor ex): fixed_damage 40, "Flip a coin. If heads, this attack does 40 more damage." The engine maps it to CoinFlipExtraDamage{extra_damage:40} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:1022-1023). coinflip_extra_damage_attack (apply_attack_action.rs:1891-1896) gives heads 40+40=80 and tails 40. Heads therefore does 80 and KOs a 30-HP Bonsly (B3 078 hp 30, lib db:66551-66555), as seen. Test promotion_continuation_tests.rs:614-655 (Exeggutor ex vs a 60-HP Bulbasaur) pins two 50% branches: heads KOs, tails does not.
result.note: The part of the claim that was actually seen (heads, 80 damage, Bonsly KO'd) matches. The claim's wording is wrong against the card text and the engine, but the error rests only on an unobserved inference. Tropical Swing does not need a coin flip to deal damage: the printed damage is 40, not 80, and tails still deals 40. That would also have KO'd a 30-HP Bonsly, so this battle doesn't show the flip mattered. Correct the claim text, not the engine.

claim: Big Beat deals 120 damage and then shows a 'next turn self-lock' indicator on the attacker, though the exact restriction it imposes on the following turn was not clearly detailed.

result.evidence: Big Beat (Buzzwole ex, lib/deckgym-database.json:23248-23251): 120, "During your next turn, this Pokémon can't use Big Beat." The engine maps it to DamageAndCardEffect{opponent:false, effect:CannotUseAttack("Big Beat"), duration:2} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:359-365). damage_and_card_effect_attack (apply_attack_action.rs:3467-3490) deals 120 and puts the effect on the attacker, lasting through its owner's next turn (played_card.rs:340-346). Move generation leaves out only the named attack (move_generation/attacks.rs:42-64), so Punch stays usable. Test tinkaton_gigaton_hammer_test.rs:58-82 pins the same self-lock pattern (Gigaton Hammer is not offered on the next turn).
result.note: The restriction the video didn't spell out is: only Big Beat is blocked on the attacker's next turn. Other attacks and actions stay available. No test covers Buzzwole ex itself.

claim: Pierce the Pain can target a damaged opposing Benched Pokémon regardless of its max HP; it dealt 100 damage to knock out a damaged Benched Gholdengo for the game-ending point, since it already had 20 damage.

result.evidence: Pierce the Pain (Decidueye ex, lib db:18057-18060): "100 damage to 1 of your opponent's Pokémon that have damage on them." The engine maps it to DirectDamageIfDamaged{damage:100} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2022-2023). direct_damage_if_damaged (apply_attack_action.rs:2806-2825) offers every opposing Pokémon in play, Active or Bench, with is_damaged(). It has no max-HP condition. Gholdengo (120 HP, A2b 057) with 20 damage has 100 left, so 100 KOs it, and the 3rd point ends the game (apply_action_helpers.rs:845-855). The same mechanic is pinned by mandibuzz_blindside_test.rs:12-69 (only the damaged benched Pokémon is a legal target, it is KO'd, and a point is scored) and :74-109 (an undamaged Active is not hit).
result.note: The pinning test uses Mandibuzz's 60-damage version of the same mechanic, not Decidueye ex itself.

claim: Pheromosa's one-Energy Jump Blues deals 20 damage to the opposing Active and 20 damage to one opposing Benched Pokemon simultaneously, hitting two separate targets in a single use.

result.evidence: Jump Blues (Pheromosa A3a 007, lib db:23271-23274): 20, "This attack also does 20 damage to 1 of your opponent's Benched Pokémon." The engine maps it to AlsoChoiceBenchDamage{opponent:true, damage:20} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:1946-1950). also_choice_bench_damage (apply_attack_action.rs:2647-2698) offers one choice per opposing benched Pokémon. Each choice is a single ApplyQueuedAttackDamage with two targets, (20 to the Active) and (20 to the chosen bench slot), applied together. With an empty bench it falls back to 20 on the Active only. Test raikou_rocky_helmet_order_test.rs:10-54 pins the same mechanic (Raikou ex, 60 + 10 to the bench): both hits resolve in one action (Active at 10, bench at 50).
result.note: The pinning test uses Raikou ex's 10-damage version of the same text family, not Pheromosa itself.

claim: Derisive Roasting deals its 10 base damage plus 50 extra per Special Condition on the target (e.g. 10+50x2=110 with two conditions present), confirmed in 3 separate uses.

result.evidence: Derisive Roasting (Team Rocket's Magmar B4a 006, lib db:80233-80236): 10, +50 "for each Special Condition affecting your opponent's Active Pokémon." The engine maps it to ExtraDamagePerOpponentSpecialCondition{damage_per_condition:50} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:1610-1614). extra_damage_per_opponent_special_condition (apply_attack_action.rs:4616-4634) counts Asleep, Burned, Confused, Paralyzed and Poisoned on the defending Active and returns 10 + 50 x count. With 2 conditions that is 110. Test b4a_simple_attack_effects_test.rs:115-140 pins 0 conditions = 10 and 3 conditions = 160.

claim: An attack's forced-switch effect (Reverse Thrust) is simply skipped with no effect if the opponent has no Benched Pokémon available to switch in.

result.evidence: Reverse Thrust (Team Rocket's Koffing B4a 042, lib db:81085-81088): 10, "Switch this Pokémon with 1 of your Benched Pokémon". It switches the attacker's own side, not the defender's. The engine maps it to SwitchSelfWithBench (effect_mechanic_map.rs:1725-1726). switch_self_with_bench (apply_attack_action.rs:5802-5829) builds switch choices from the attacker's own bench. With none, it deals the 10 damage and pushes nothing, so the switch is silently skipped. The battle review (Pocket Deck Lab/Boss Folder/wsl-review-campaign-2026-09-22/battle-20260922-010316/REVIEW.md:19) confirms that at T7 the Koffing user (Dustin's opponent) had no Bench.
result.note: Calling it a 'forced switch' is misleading, because Reverse Thrust switches the attacker's own Pokémon. 'The opponent' in the claim is the Koffing user, and their empty Bench is what made the switch impossible. Read that way, the engine matches. No test covers the empty-bench case for this exact function. The nearest test is test_volt_switch_offers_nothing_without_a_lightning_bench (switch_and_gust_attacks_test.rs:76-92), which covers the Volt Switch version.

claim: Overlord's Blade deals damage scaling with the attacker's own number of Pokémon KO'd (180 damage for 3 KOs), a count tracked separately from the opponent's point total (only 2, after a coin flip denied one point).

result.evidence: Overlord's Blade (Kingambit B3a 043, lib db:71037-71040): 60 + 40 "for each time your Pokémon have been Knocked Out during this game." The engine maps it to ExtraDamagePerOwnKnockoutThisGame{40} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:3357-3358). apply_attack_action.rs:4719-4726 uses state.own_knockouts_this_game[attacker]. That count goes up for every KO in handle_knockouts (apply_action_helpers.rs:766), after and regardless of the point award, including when DenyKnockoutPoints zeroes the points (apply_action_helpers.rs:718-733). So 3 own KOs with only 2 opponent points gives 60+120=180. Test kingambit_overlords_blade_test.rs:13-53 (0 KOs = 60) and :60-107 (1 KO = 100) pins the scaling.
result.note: The Kingambit test sets the counter directly (set_own_knockouts_this_game). No test pins the case where a point-denied KO still counts. That part comes from reading the code at apply_action_helpers.rs:718-766, and it matches rules/02_damage_knockouts_points.md:112 [OBSERVED 181914].

claim: Sitrus Berry heals 30 HP once its holder is at or below half Max HP, resolving at the end of the opponent's turn rather than immediately, then is discarded; two Berries on one Pokémon resolve sequentially (20→50→80 HP), each discarding after healing.

result.evidence: Sitrus Berry resolves only in the end-of-turn hook, never when damage lands. engine/src/hooks/core.rs:2240-2287 (apply_end_of_turn_berries_for_owner) runs for the player ending the turn (core.rs:416) and for the other player (core.rs:573-574). So a Pokémon damaged by the opponent's attack heals at the end of that opponent's turn. The eligibility check is remaining*2 <= effective max HP (core.rs:2270), which means 'at or below half'. The order is heal 30 (core.rs:2277), then discard that one Berry (core.rs:2282), and the loop repeats for a second copy. The exact 20->50->80 sequence on a 120-HP B4 115 Revavroom is pinned by engine/tests/revavroom_assumptions_test.rs:50-73 (100 damage, two Sitrus -> 80 HP, both discarded). The single-Berry heal+discard is pinned by engine/tests/tools/berries_test.rs:92-122.
result.note: The engine fires Sitrus at the end of EVERY turn, the owner's included, not only the opponent's. That agrees with the card text ('At the end of each turn') and does not conflict with the claim, which only says the heal is delayed rather than immediate.

claim: A pending end-of-turn Sitrus Berry heal does not occur if its holder is Knocked Out first; a Revavroom holding two Sitrus Berries was KO'd in one hit (130 dmg vs 120 HP) before either Berry could heal.

result.evidence: Attack damage KOs are resolved inside the attack. handle_damage (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:495-514) calls handle_knockouts. That discards the KO'd Pokémon with all its Tools via discard_from_play (apply_action_helpers.rs:795) before EndTurn is reached, so no Sitrus holder remains for the end-of-turn hook. The hook also skips KO'd holders explicitly (!pokemon.is_knocked_out(), core.rs:2266). A test pins that a 0-HP pending-KO Sitrus holder is not healed and keeps the Berry until discarded: engine/tests/rules_repair_end_turn.rs:9-99. Tools going to discard on KO is pinned by engine/tests/tools/tools_integration_test.rs:232-265. B4 115 Revavroom has 120 HP (card DB), so 130 damage KOs it in the engine too.
result.note: No test covers the exact attack-KO-of-a-Sitrus-holder scenario, but the code path is unambiguous.

claim: Whether Sitrus Berry's half-Max-HP eligibility re-checks after each sequential heal (two Berries) or is captured once before both resolve is undetermined; the one observed case (healing to 50 of 120 Max HP) fits either reading.

result.evidence: The engine takes the re-check side. After every successful Berry it re-evaluates remaining*2 <= max HP (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:2262-2285, comment at 2268-2269). It is pinned by engine/tests/revavroom_assumptions_test.rs:30-47: 70 damage, two Sitrus -> 50 HP -> 80 HP, second Berry stays attached. The engine labels this 'Owner-approved assumption, not verified in Pokémon TCG Pocket' (engine/src/card_validation.rs:93). The observed 20->50->80 case gives the same result under either reading, so the footage cannot confirm or refute the engine's choice.
result.note: A recording of a two-Sitrus Revavroom ending a turn with 31-60 HP remaining (of 120) would settle it. Re-check reading (engine): +30 once, one Berry left. Capture-once reading: +60, both Berries gone. Example: 50 HP gives 80 with one Berry left, versus 110.

claim: Lucky Ice Pop heals a flat 20 HP, capped at max HP (e.g. 60→70 not 80 near cap), then flips a coin: Heads returns it to hand for reuse (sometimes same turn), Tails discards it; confirmed repeatedly across many battles.

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:725-755 (lucky_ice_pop_outcomes). Both heads and tails branches heal 20 from the Active. On heads the card is moved from discard back to hand (lines 735-748); on tails it stays discarded. The heal is capped at current damage: heal_raw uses saturating_sub on damage counters (engine/src/state/played_card.rs:227-229; state/mod.rs:863-873), so 60/70 -> 70. Items have no per-turn limit (move_generation_trainer.rs:23-27), so a returned Pop can be replayed the same turn while the Active is still damaged (move_generation_trainer.rs:452-459). Pinned by engine/tests/tools/lucky_ice_pop_test.rs:37-57 (always heals 20) and :60-105 (heads -> hand, tails -> discard, both occur).
result.note: The engine offers Lucky Ice Pop only when the Active is damaged. The flip is skipped only when the heal is 0 (Heal Block), which matches 'If you healed any damage'.

claim: An HP-boosting Tool's bonus (Giant Cape: +20 max HP) is added to base HP and persists through evolution, updating Max HP to match (80-HP Brionne+Giant Cape became 200-HP Primarina ex = 180+20); current HP also rises by the same amount on attachment (Arceus ex 140→160), confirmed on multiple Pokémon.

result.evidence: Max HP is computed live as base_hp + tool bonuses (engine/src/state/played_card.rs:290-310; Giant Cape +20 at line 295). Remaining HP = max HP - damage counters (played_card.rs:276-279), so attaching a Cape raises current HP by the same 20 (Arceus ex 140 -> 160). On evolution, apply_evolve copies attached_tools and damage onto the new card with the evolved card's base HP (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1521-1528). Brionne 80 + Cape therefore becomes Primarina ex 180 + 20 = 200. Attach raising current HP is pinned by engine/tests/tools/tools_integration_test.rs:30-66. Stacking is pinned by engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:128-147 and :173-193.
result.note: No test pins Cape-through-evolution directly; it is code-only (apply_action.rs:1524). Elegant Cape (listed in cards) is gated on the holder being Stage 1 (played_card.rs:299-301). So its +30 would drop if a Stage 1 evolves to Stage 2: 'persists through evolution' holds for Giant Cape, not for Elegant Cape in that case.

claim: Heavy Helmet's printed damage reduction (conditional on the holder's Retreat Cost being 3 or higher) was never confirmed actually applying against an attack in this footage; the holder (Kingambit) was never attacked before the match ended.

result.evidence: This claim records an absence of evidence, not a behavior. The engine does implement Heavy Helmet: -20 per Helmet against opponent attack damage when the holder's printed Retreat Cost has 3 or more entries (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:702-713). This is pinned by unit test core.rs:2872-2879 (Snorlax 40 -> 20) and engine/tests/rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:69 (attack-only). Kingambit (B3a 043) has Retreat Cost 3, so the engine would apply -20 had it been attacked.
result.note: Settle with footage of a Heavy-Helmeted Pokémon with Retreat Cost 3 or more (e.g. Kingambit) taking an opponent's attack, compared against printed damage minus 20. The engine reads the PRINTED retreat cost (retreat_cost.len()), so Retreat Cost changes (Peculiar Plaza etc.) do not switch it off. That is still open in rules/05 #19 and rules/08 T8.

claim: Playing a new Stadium card immediately removes and replaces whichever Stadium is currently in play; only one Stadium can be active at a time (Area Zero replaced Mesagoza on turn 9).

result.evidence: Playing a Stadium calls set_active_stadium_for_player, which swaps the single active_stadium slot. The old Stadium goes to its original player's discard pile at once (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:977-987; engine/src/state/mod.rs:585-593). HP bonuses are then refreshed and knockouts checked. Only one Stadium slot exists (State.active_stadium). Pinned by engine/tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:262-317 (Training Area replaces Peculiar Plaza; Plaza goes to player 0's discard).
result.note: Side note, not in the claim: has_used_stadium is tracked per player per turn, not per Stadium card. If Mesagoza had already been used that turn, the engine would not let the same player use the new Area Zero until their next turn.

claim: Field Blower discards one targeted opposing Pokémon Tool (chosen among several if multiple are attached), permanently removing its effect; removing an HP-boosting Tool immediately drops the holder's current and max HP by that Tool's bonus (Primarina ex 200→180; another case 150→130). Confirmed removing Small Balloon and Heavy Helmet too.

result.evidence: Field Blower pushes one choice per attached Tool index on every Pokémon (both players), plus the Stadium (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:578-602). The chosen Tool is removed via discard_tool (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1267-1273). Because max HP is recomputed live from attached_tools (played_card.rs:290-310) and remaining = max - damage, removing Giant Cape drops both current and max HP by 20 (200->180, 150->130). If damage is at or above the new max, the holder is KO'd. Pinned by engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:225-269 (each Tool offered, only the selected index removed), :272-313 (removing a Cape causes KO), and engine/tests/trainers/field_blower_test.rs:21-86 (opponent's Tool discarded). Small Balloon and Heavy Helmet are removed by the same generic path.
result.note: The engine also lets Field Blower target your own Tools or the Stadium (matches the card text); the claim describes only the opposing-Tool use.

claim: Rocky Helmet deals 20 damage back to the attacker whenever its holder is Knocked Out by that attack; observed triggering for 20 after Heatmor was KO'd, taking the attacker from 100 to 80 HP.

result.evidence: Rocky Helmet adds 20 per copy to counterattack damage (engine/src/hooks/counterattack.rs:13-17). It is applied in handle_attack_retaliation (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:593-612) BEFORE handle_knockouts (apply_action_helpers.rs:512-513), so it fires even when its holder is KO'd by that attack. Pinned by engine/tests/observed_gameplay_outcomes_test.rs:115-160 (Sudowoodo with Rocky Helmet KO'd by Psychic; attacker Exeggutor 130 -> 110). Heatmor (80 HP) KO'd with the attacker going 100 -> 80 follows the same path.
result.note: The engine trigger is broader than 'when KO'd'. Per the card text it fires whenever the holder is damaged by an opponent's attack while in the Active Spot (damaged_actives only records index 0, apply_action_helpers.rs:585-587), whether or not it is KO'd. The claim is correct for the KO case but should not be read as KO-only.

claim: Soothing Shore (Stadium) heals the damaged Active 20 HP at end of turn, independent of any Pokémon ability, but only if that Active still has Water Energy attached; twice the Active had none (stripped by Air Crash) and received no heal.

result.evidence: apply_soothing_shore_healing (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:607-616), called at core.rs:569. At the end of a player's turn it heals 20 from each of THAT player's Pokémon whose attached_energy contains Water. It is a Stadium effect independent of Abilities, and a Pokémon with no Water Energy gets nothing. Pinned by engine/tests/stadiums/soothing_shore_test.rs:25-82 (W-Energy Active heals; non-W bench and the other player do not) and :85-115 (the other player heals when their own turn ends).
result.note: The engine heals only at the end of the Stadium user's OWN turn and heals Benched W-Energy Pokémon too, not just the Active. In the Wailord case the energy was stripped by the opponent's Air Crash (Corviknight ex, 'Discard a random Energy from your opponent's Active Pokémon'). The engine would give no heal both at the end of the opponent's turn (wrong player) and at the end of Wailord's owner's turn if it still had no W Energy, so either timing is consistent.

claim: Rainbow Cave (Stadium) discards the Energy Zone's currently generated Energy and advances to a newly generated (queued) type, which the player then manually attaches; it never attaches Energy directly itself and is not a free pick of any type (e.g. Fighting→Metal observed).

result.evidence: forecast_rainbow_cave_effect (engine/src/actions/apply_stadium_action.rs:78-93) moves energy_zone.current into the Energy discard pile and calls rotate_energy_zone (engine/src/state/mod.rs:931-940). That promotes the previewed 'next' Energy to current and rolls a fresh random 'next' from the deck's Energy types. It does not attach anything and gives no free type choice. It needs a current Energy to exist and can be used once per turn (engine/src/stadiums.rs:201-205). Pinned by engine/tests/stadiums/rainbow_cave_test.rs:45-78 (Fire discarded, previewed Water becomes current), :81-90 (unavailable once the Energy is attached), and :93-111 (the new Energy is then attached by the normal turn attach).

claim: A single Pokémon can have more than one Pokémon Tool attached at once, in separate Tool slots; one Revavroom held two Sitrus Berry Tools simultaneously.

result.evidence: Tool capacity is 1 by default and 2 only for a Pokémon with the ToolCapacity ability (engine/src/tools.rs:112-133). That ability is mapped from Dual Customization's text 'This Pokémon may have up to 2 Pokémon Tool cards attached to it.' (engine/src/actions/effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:20-23), which only B4 115 Revavroom has. Two separate Tools are stored in attached_tools, and identical copies are allowed. Pinned by engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:97-125 (second Tool allowed, third refused), :128-147 (two identical Tools through legal play), and engine/tests/revavroom_assumptions_test.rs:50-73 (two Sitrus Berries on one Revavroom).
result.note: This is true only for Dual Customization Revavroom. The engine keeps one Tool per Pokémon for everything else, including other Revavroom printings (pinned by revavroom_tools_test.rs:150-170), which matches rules/04 line 96. Read as a general rule ('a single Pokémon can have more than one Tool'), the claim would be an overgeneralization.

claim: Team Rocket Grunt flips a coin per potentially-removable Energy and discards 1 opposing Energy per Heads, capped at the amount actually attached (e.g. 3 Heads only removed 2 attached Energy); 0 Heads removes 0.

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2511-2540 (team_rocket_grunt_outcomes): coin flips run until the first tails. The effect is saturated at K = number of Energy on the opponent's Active (line 2514-2517), and each heads discards one random Energy (rng.gen_range, lines 2521-2535), stopping when none are left. engine/src/actions/outcomes.rs:138-170 (saturated_geometric_classes): 0..K-1 heads each form an exact H^n T branch, and the last branch covers every H^n T with n >= K and applies make_mutation(K). So 3 heads against 2 attached Energy discards exactly 2, and 0 heads (a single tails) discards 0. Playability: move_generation_trainer.rs:1008-1023 requires the opponent's Active to have at least 1 Energy. No integration test pins this card.
result.note: The claim's wording 'flips a coin per potentially-removable Energy' is wrong: the card text and the engine both say flip until tails. The observation itself (3 heads followed by tails, with only 2 Energy attached) fits flip-until-tails and does not fit one flip per Energy. The discard outcome matches the engine. rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/trainers.md:263 agrees.

claim: Metal Core Barrier reduces one incoming attack's damage by exactly 50 (e.g. Wild Swing 60→10, Mega Blaster 140→90), flooring at 0 not negative, then is discarded at the end of the holder's opponent's following turn, unless the holder is KO'd first.

result.evidence: Reduction: engine/src/hooks/core.rs:715-735 (get_metal_core_barrier_reduction) gives -50 per Barrier, only for attack damage and only when the holder is [M] type. Floor at 0: core.rs:1883-1885 subtracts with saturating_sub after Weakness. Test engine/tests/rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:172-202 pins 60 Fire into Skarmory ex with Barrier under Bounded Field = 70, and 10 damage -> 0 (floor). Discard timing: core.rs:504-519 runs at the end of each turn and removes Barriers from the Pokémon of the player who is NOT ending the turn, which is the holder's opponent's turn. Test engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:663-681 pins both Barriers going to the discard pile when the opponent (player 1) ends their turn. Non-Metal gate: engine/tests/tools/tool_effect_gating_test.rs:35-56. If the holder is KO'd, its Tools go to the discard pile with it (state/mod.rs:1252-1263).
result.note: Corviknight ex and Aegislash are both Metal, so the [M] gate is met. Wild Swing 60->10 and Mega Blaster 140->90 are Water attacks into non-Water-weak holders, so -50 applies straight. 'One incoming attack' is true in practice because the opponent gets only one attack before the Barrier expires. The engine doesn't count attacks; it reduces every attack while the Barrier is attached.

claim: Starting Plains (Stadium) raises every Basic Pokémon's max HP by 20 for both players (e.g. Mega Diancie ex 120→140, Castform +20); higher-stage Pokémon (Stage 2 Mega Blaziken, Aegislash) are unaffected. This raised threshold let combined attack + Burn Checkup damage reach a KO.

result.evidence: engine/src/state/played_card.rs:257-267 (refresh_starting_plains_bonus) gives stadium_hp_bonus = 20 only when stage == BASIC_STAGE. It is added to effective max HP at played_card.rs:306, and remaining HP = effective max - damage (played_card.rs:276-279), so remaining HP also rises by 20. engine/src/state/mod.rs:607-609 (refresh_hp_bonuses_all) applies it to both players. Tests: engine/tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:478-516 (own Basics +20, Stage 1 Ivysaur unchanged) and 518-586 (opponent's Basic Bulbasaur has 90 HP under Plains; 80 damage leaves 10). KO checks use effective HP (played_card.rs:281-283).

claim: Flame Patch (Item) attaches a Fire Energy taken from the discard pile onto the Active Pokémon (e.g. 1→2 Fire) without consuming that turn's normal once-per-turn generated Energy attachment; usable repeatedly to rebuild Energy after a KO (used twice in one battle).

Kid's Room was already used at 2:08-2:40 of the same video, so the 3:02 block was most likely an attempt to use it, and the engine blocks that. Activate goes through apply_retreat(..., is_free=true) and then straight to apply_activate, with no Energy discarded and has_retreated not set (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:823-830, 1431-1435). result.note: The code matches every part of the claim. There is no dedicated test.

claim: A Pokemon holding Elegant Cape retreats for 0 Energy cost, confirmed on 2 separate retreats with no Energy discarded.

result.evidence: The engine reproduces the observed free retreats, but not because of Elegant Cape. Mega Sharpedo ex (B4 035) has retreat_cost [] in engine/database.json, and the printed card also says retreat 0 (lib/deckgym-database.json). No retreat-cost code mentions Elegant Cape (engine/src/hooks/retreat.rs:118-251).
result.note: The claim gets the cause wrong. The free retreat comes from Mega Sharpedo ex's printed Retreat Cost of 0, not from Elegant Cape. In the engine (and per the card text), a Pokémon with Retreat Cost 1 or more holding Elegant Cape still pays in full. The recorded events match the engine; the general rule in the claim does not. Mega Sharpedo ex is Stage 1, so the Cape also gives it +30 HP (190 -> 220).

claim: Sabrina forces the opponent's Active Pokémon to switch to the Bench at no retreat cost, but the affected opponent (not the Sabrina player) chooses which Benched Pokémon replaces it; confirmed across at least three battles.

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:841-854 (sabrina_effect) builds Activate{player: opponent} choices for every opponent Benched Pokémon. It pushes them on the stack for opponent_player (line 853), so the affected opponent chooses, not the Sabrina player. Activate is free: no Energy is discarded and it doesn't count as a retreat (apply_action.rs:823-830, 1431-1435). Playability: move_generation_trainer.rs:625-634 requires at least 1 opponent Benched Pokémon. engine/tests/rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:37-60 plays Sabrina through the full game API, but with only one Benched target, so it doesn't pin who chooses.
result.note: The chooser is correct in the code (rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/trainers.md:220 agrees), but no test has two or more Benched targets and checks that the opponent picks.

claim: Psychic Supporter moves one randomly-selected Energy attached to an opponent's Benched Pokemon onto their Active, observed changing Numel 5→4 Fire and Moltres 1→2 Fire.

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2134-2145 (psychic_effect): the Psychic player chooses one of the opponent's Benched Pokémon that has Energy (card_logic/psychic.rs:18-27). Then SimpleAction::MoveRandomOpponentEnergyToActive moves 1 Energy from it to the opponent's Active (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:928-933, then apply_move_last_energy at 998-1005). Test engine/tests/trainers/psychic_test.rs:16-69 pins bench 2 Fire -> 1 Fire and Active 0 -> 1 Fire, with the Psychic player choosing the source.

It always moves the last-attached Energy (apply_action.rs:930-932 has a code comment saying this was done to avoid expanding the game tree). Here the Benched Numel had only Fire, so 5->4 Fire and Moltres 1->2 Fire come out the same. The difference only shows when a Benched Pokémon has mixed Energy types. rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/trainers.md:207 says this card 'is correctly random'; the current code shows that is wrong.

claim: Pokémon Center Lady heals exactly 30 HP (e.g. Moltres 70→100), stacking additively with other same-turn heals; its Special-Condition-recovery clause has no visible effect when the target has no Special Condition to cure, but the 30-HP heal still applies regardless.

Tests: engine/tests/s180_e1_fixtures.rs:271-277 (c4: 50 damage, no status -> heals exactly 30), 291-301 (c6: heals 30 and clears Poisoned+Asleep); engine/tests/s182_e1_center_lady_targets.rs:75-127 (target legality).

claim: Peculiar Plaza (Stadium) reduces Psychic-type retreat cost by 2; a Psychic Pokemon with 0 attached Energy retreated for free with no Energy discarded.

result.evidence: engine/src/stadiums.rs:119-127 gives a reduction of 2 for any Psychic-type Pokémon while Peculiar Plaza is the active Stadium, for both players. engine/src/hooks/retreat.rs:207-218 pops that many cost entries, and popping an empty cost does nothing, so the cost floors at 0. A 0-cost retreat discards nothing (apply_action.rs:1431-1467). Tests: engine/tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:29-86 (Mewtwo, retreat 2, 0 Energy: no retreat before Plaza, retreat offered after) and 163-222 (applies to both players).

result.evidence: Test engine/tests/b4a_basculegion_soul_counter_test.rs:183-200 (point_denial_also_denies_iris_bonus...) shows a Haxorus KO of a non-ex Active (Glimmora) with Iris played that turn scores exactly 2 points (1 base + 1 Iris), the same 0-to-2 jump seen in the video. engine/tests/trainers/iris_trainer_test.rs:10-51 and b4a_basculegion_soul_counter_test.rs:173-181 cover the ex case (2+1=3). claim: Clemont's Backpack adds +20 damage to that turn's attack, including printed Bench-spread damage (e.g. 10→30 per Benched Pokémon); copies stack additively (2 copies = +40), and the bonus expires by the following turn.

result.evidence: Bench bonus: test engine/tests/rules_repair_damage_opening.rs:134-170 shows Heliolisk Electrispark after Clemont's Backpack does 30 to a Benched Pokemon (10+20), while Giovanni still gives 10. The code lets the Backpack skip the Active-only gate (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:1069-1087, is_backpack at 1074-1078). Stacking: each Backpack pushes its own TurnEffect entry with no de-duplication (apply_trainer_action.rs:2355-2364; state/mod.rs:1063-1078 pushes clones). get_increased_turn_effect_modifiers sums every entry (core.rs:1038-1113, .sum at 1113), so 2 copies = +40. Item play is unrestricted (move_generation_trainer.rs:261 -> can_play_trainer at :23-27). Expiry: duration 0 stores the effect only under the current turn_count (state/mod.rs:1064-1069), and get_current_turn_effects reads only that turn (mod.rs:1081-1086), so the bonus is gone on the next turn.

The Backpack is detected by its numbers (+20 for Magneton/Heliolisk), which is fragile, as rules/10 R4 notes. The bonus applies only to Magneton or Heliolisk attacks, as the card text says.

claim: Training Area (Stadium) adds a flat +10 damage to attacks that hit the opposing Active Pokémon, for both players' qualifying attacks (not just its owner's); it does not apply to attacks targeting a Benched Pokémon (e.g. no bonus on Electrode's Bench-targeting Random Spark).

result.evidence: get_training_area_damage_bonus returns +10 for any Stage 1 attacker, with no player or owner filter (engine/src/stadiums.rs:129-137; has_stadium at stadiums.rs:106-113 checks only which Stadium is in play). The bonus is added only when is_active_to_active holds, that is target_idx==0 && attacking_idx==0 && from an attack (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:1737, 1817-1832). Random Spark (Team Rocket's Electrode B4a 020, Stage 1, 30 to 1 opposing Pokemon) is Mechanic::DirectDamage (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2198-2202). It deals its damage through ApplyDamage aimed at the chosen in_play_idx (apply_attack_action.rs:2768-2775), so a Bench target (idx != 0) gets no Training Area bonus. Tests: engine/tests/stadiums/stadium_test.rs:323-379 (Stage 1 +10), :381-423 (Basic not boosted), :425+ (Stage 2 not boosted), :682-722 (Training Area in play with no owner still boosts the attacker).
result.note: No test covers the Bench exclusion or a real opponent-owned Stadium. Those two parts are checked from the code only (no owner filter; the gate at core.rs:1819). All the attackers named in the evidence are Stage 1 per the DB (Mega Altaria ex, Mega Manectric ex, Combusken, Heliolisk, TR Electrode). The claim's 'qualifying attacks' means attacks by Stage 1 Pokemon.

claim: Elegant Cape raises max HP by 30 once its holder is Stage 1 or higher (none while Basic), persisting through evolution (Electrike→Mega Manectric ex: 210=180+30); on a damaged Pokémon it raises current HP by 30 too (110→140), and that buffer erodes with further damage (140→120).

result.evidence: HP bonus: played_card.rs:299-301 adds +30 per Elegant Cape only when the holder's stage == 1. Remaining HP = effective max - damage_counters (played_card.rs:276-279, 290-310). So on a damaged holder the remaining HP rises by the same 30 (130-max TR Slowking ex at 110 -> 140 of 160), and later damage wears it down normally (apply_damage only adds counters, played_card.rs:231-233). Attaching does nothing else to HP (apply_action.rs:966-994). Evolution: apply_evolve keeps the damage counters and copies attached_tools to the new card (apply_action.rs:1521-1524). Electrike (60, Basic) -> Mega Manectric ex (180, Stage 1) therefore gives 180+30=210. Tests: engine/tests/tools/tool_effect_gating_test.rs:24-33 (a Basic holder gets no bonus), engine/tests/tools/tools_integration_test.rs:68-123 (Stage 1 holder +30).
result.note: One wording mismatch. The claim says 'Stage 1 or higher', but the card text (B3b 065, 'The Stage 1 Pokemon...') and the engine (stage == 1 exactly) give no bonus to a Stage 2 holder. Every observed holder was Stage 1 (Mega Manectric ex, TR Slowking ex, Silvally), so nothing observed contradicts the engine. The 'or higher' is an overgeneralization, not a finding. No test pins the evolution-carryover number (210).

claim: Misty requires a coin flip to attach Energy to its target; a Tails (0 Heads) result attaches no Energy that use, confirmed across separate observations.

result.evidence: Misty flips until the first tails, as a real sequence of coin flips (engine/src/actions/trainer_coin_plan.rs:526-536, sample_until_tails). It then attaches one Water Energy per heads, and only if heads > 0 (trainer_coin_plan.rs:393-397 in sample_misty_target_actual, :363-403). A first-flip tails gives 0 heads and attaches nothing. The target is chosen before any coin is flipped (apply_trainer_action.rs:817-831 stages the target; tests engine/tests/misty_precoin_target_test.rs:164-185).
result.note: No test asserts the exact case '0 heads -> 0 Energy'. misty_precoin_target_test.rs:164-185 only requires that heads show up in some seeds. The 0-Energy result follows directly from the heads>0 guard and the H*T sampler. Energy comes from the Energy Zone and does not use up the manual attachment.

claim: Irida heals 40 HP on its target Pokemon.

result.evidence: irida_effect heals 40 (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:528-534) through state.heal_each_pokemon (state/mod.rs:877-891). Card text (A2a 072): 'Heal 40 damage from each of your Pokemon that has any [W] Energy attached.' Irida can be played only when at least one damaged Pokemon has Water Energy (move_generation_trainer.rs:489+).
result.note: The 40 amount matches. The claim's 'its target Pokemon' is looser than both the card and the engine: there is no target choice, and 40 is healed from every one of your Pokemon that has Water Energy attached. The result looks the same when only one such Pokemon is damaged. If the video showed a Pokemon with no Water Energy being healed, or a damaged Water-Energy Pokemon left unhealed, that would be a contradiction. The claim gives no such detail. No engine test covers Irida.

claim: Team Rocket's Goo-zooka raises the opponent's retreat cost by 1 for that turn.

result.evidence: team_rockets_goozooka_effect puts CardEffect::IncreasedRetreatCost{amount:1} with duration 1 on the opponent's Active (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:421-427). Test engine/tests/b4a_trainer_batch2_test.rs:159-190 shows a Blastoise with 3 Energy can't retreat on the opponent's next turn (cost 3+1) and can retreat again on the turn after. :192-219 shows both printings share the effect.
result.note: The card text says 'Until the end of your opponent's next turn'. The claim's 'for that turn' can only mean the opponent's following turn, since the opponent can't retreat during the Goo-zooka player's own turn. The engine ties the effect to the Pokemon in the opponent's Active Spot, not to the Spot itself.

claim: Team Rocket's Thieving Machine retrieves a card (a Trainer card observed) specifically from the opponent's discard pile, not the player's own, moving it to the user's hand to replay.

result.evidence: team_rockets_thieving_machine_outcomes builds its pool only from state.discard_piles[opponent]: Item cards other than Thieving Machine (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:386-396). It picks one uniformly at random, removes it from the opponent's discard and pushes it into hands[actor] (:401-414). Tests: engine/tests/b4a_trainer_batch2_test.rs:84-106 (Potion moves from opponent's discard to player 0's hand; the Supporter stays), :108-139 (random among eligible Items only), :141-157 (not playable when there's no eligible Item).
result.note: The claim says 'a Trainer card'. The engine and the card restrict this to Item cards. The card seen, Poke Ball, is an Item, so this is consistent. The stolen card sits in the thief's hand and can be played like any card in hand.

claim: Pokemon Flute returns a previously Knocked Out Pokemon from the discard pile directly onto the Bench, not to hand.

result.evidence: Pokemon Flute (A1a 064: 'Put a Basic Pokemon from your opponent's discard pile onto their Bench') offers BenchOpponentFromDiscard choices (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:202, :1546-1549), which apply_bench_opponent_from_discard carries out (apply_action.rs:880-882). Test engine/tests/trainers/disruption_items_test.rs:217-255 shows a Basic (Squirtle) moving from the opponent's discard onto the opponent's Bench and leaving the discard. :257-298 show the card is blocked with no Basic in the discard or with a full Bench.
result.note: The engine matches 'onto the Bench, not to hand'. The card's discard and Bench are both the opponent's (the side of the Flute player's opponent). The claim doesn't say whose, and only Basics qualify.

claim: Professor Turo shuffles the opponent's own damaged Active Pokemon into the deck rather than to discard or hand.

result.evidence: professor_turo_effect offers ShuffleInPlayPokemonIntoDeck for any of the player's own in-play Future Pokemon, Active included (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:634-649). Test engine/tests/trainers/professor_turo_test.rs:21-87 chooses the Active Future Pokemon (Iron Hands) and asserts the card ends up in the deck (decks[0].cards contains it) and a promotion is then required. :89-141 shows that with no Bench the player loses.
result.note: 'The opponent's own' here means the opponent played Turo on their own Pokemon, which matches the card ('1 of your Future Pokemon'). The engine lets any Future Pokemon be shuffled in, damaged or not, so the damage doesn't matter.

claim: Steel Apron is a persistent Tool (stays attached across multiple turns, unlike the one-turn Metal Core Barrier), reducing all incoming attack damage by 10 and granting its holder immunity to Special Conditions.

result.evidence: -10: get_steel_apron_reduction applies to damage from an opponent's attack, on any target slot, only when the holder is Metal type (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:737-762). Immunity: apply_status_condition returns early for a Metal holder (state/mod.rs:1151-1158), and attaching the Apron cures existing conditions (apply_action.rs:982-993). Persistence: Steel Apron has no discard path. Metal Core Barrier is the only one of the two discarded at the end of the opponent's turn (core.rs:504-519). Tests: engine/tests/steel_apron_test.rs:160-187 (40 -> 30), :133-158 (no new conditions), :87-131 (cured on attach), :57-85 (no reduction on a non-Metal holder).
result.note: The engine gives all effects only to a [M] holder, as the card text says. The claim doesn't state the holder's type. 'All incoming attack damage' means attack damage from the opponent's Pokemon; the engine does not reduce self-damage or non-attack damage. No test checks that the Apron is still attached several turns later; that is checked from the code only (no discard path).

claim: Leftovers heals its holder 10 HP repeatedly across turns and stacks additively with other same-turn healing (Potion's 20 then Leftovers' 10 took a Pokemon from 40 to 70).

result.evidence: on_end_turn (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:381) heals 10 per Leftovers from the ending player's Active at every end of that player's turn, and never discards the tool (core.rs:401-411). Potion heals 20 during the turn (apply_trainer_action.rs:667-669). Both lower damage_counters (heal_raw, played_card.rs:227-229), so they add up in order: Potion 40->60 during the turn, then Leftovers 60->70 at end of turn. Test engine/tests/tools/memory_light_leftovers_lucky_mittens_test.rs:95-132 shows +10 at end of turn.
result.note: The engine heals only when the holder is in the Active Spot at the end of its owner's turn, as the card text (A3b 067) says. The claim doesn't state that condition, but it matches an Active holder. No test covers Potion and Leftovers in the same turn or healing over several turns; both are checked from the code only.

claim: Returning a Pokémon to hand (via Ilima) drops all its attached Tools and Energy; they do not return to hand with it.

result.evidence: Ilima (apply_trainer_action.rs:1836-1846) queues SimpleAction::ReturnPokemonToHand, which apply_return_pokemon_to_hand (actions/apply_action.rs:1173-1188) resolves. Only the Pokémon card and its cards_behind (the earlier evolution stages) go to hand. attached_tools goes to discard_piles (line 1180) and attached_energy goes to discard_energies (line 1181). The test revavroom_tools_test.rs:466-501 (return_and_shuffle_actions_conserve_tools_and_energy) pins this for ReturnPokemonToHand: Giant Cape and Rocky Helmet end in the discard, the Metal Energy ends in discard_energies, and only the Pokémon ends in hand. Ilima's own tests (tests/trainers/ilima_test.rs) cover only promotion and the last-Pokémon loss.
result.note: Leaving play this way is not a Knock Out, so Lucky Egg (knock-out trigger only) correctly does nothing; the Lucky Egg card just goes to the discard. Ilima's targets are damaged [C] Pokémon only (card_logic/ilima.rs:3-11). Arceus qualifies.

claim: Rocky Helmet deals 20 damage back to any Pokémon that attacks its holder, as a Tool effect rather than an opponent attack, regardless of whether that damage is lethal to the holder; confirmed repeatedly across multiple battles.

result.evidence: Rocky Helmet's 20 comes from hooks/counterattack.rs:13-17 (20 per copy). handle_attack_retaliation (actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:592-612) applies it with attacker.apply_damage(counter_damage) at :603-605. That call skips modify_damage, so Weakness, attack boosts and 'takes -X from attacks' reductions do not touch it. It fires only for damaged_actives, meaning the opponent's attack hit the Active (apply_action_helpers.rs:585-587). Retaliation runs before handle_knockouts (attack_outcome.rs:180-209; the ResolveAttackRetaliation path is apply_action.rs:551-561), so it fires even when the holder is Knocked Out. Tests: observed_gameplay_outcomes_test.rs:184-207 (a lethal hit on a 20-HP Lucario holder still returns 20: Exeggutor 90→70) and :163-182 (non-lethal: 110→90). raikou_rocky_helmet_order_test.rs:10 covers a Helmet Knock Out during a multi-hit attack.
result.note: Ordering also matches rules/02:98: attack damage, then the attack's own effects, then Tool retaliation, then Knock Outs. Steel Wing-style '-20 from attacks' effects cannot reduce the Helmet damage, because that damage never goes through modify_damage.

claim: Cursed Jewel deals 80 direct damage and grants a delayed 'if damaged by an attack, deal 40 to the attacker' effect; if the holder is already Knocked Out, that effect never triggers.

result.evidence: Mega Sableye ex (B3b 041) Cursed Jewel maps through effect_mechanic_map.rs:544-550 to DamageAndCardEffect { opponent:false, effect: Counterattack{40}, duration:1 }: 80 printed damage, plus a 40 counterattack armed on Sableye itself for the opponent's next turn. counterattack.rs:19-27 adds the armed amount at the same retaliation point Rocky Helmet uses. Tests: public_reply_counterattack_test.rs:187-212 and :214-261 (Counterattack 40 armed for duration 1 after an 80-damage hit). public_reply.rs:899-946 reproduces the recorded case: Cursed Jewel Knocks Out the target, that ends the game, the 40 stays armed and never fires. The armed-effect trigger and its expiry are pinned on the same code path by alolan_sandslash_spike_armor_test.rs:11-67 and :69+.
result.note: This matches if 'already Knocked Out' means Sableye has left play before any attack hits it: the effect is stored on that Pokémon and is discarded with it. The clip itself only showed the game ending right after the Cursed Jewel Knock Out, and the engine reproduces that. The other reading is 'Sableye is Knocked Out by the very attack that should trigger it'. In that case the engine would still deal the 40, because retaliation runs before Knock Outs (apply_action_helpers.rs:593-612 via get_active_effects, played_card.rs:348), just as it does for Rocky Helmet. The recording never showed that case, so nothing contradicts the engine on that point.

claim: Team Rocket's Goo-zooka raises the opponent's Active Retreat Cost by 1, lasting through the opponent's next turn.

result.evidence: team_rockets_goozooka_effect (apply_trainer_action.rs:421-427) puts CardEffect::IncreasedRetreatCost{amount:1} with duration 1 on the opponent's Active. hooks/retreat.rs:220-232 adds 1 Colorless to that Pokémon's Retreat Cost. Test: b4a_trainer_batch2_test.rs:159-190. A 3-retreat Blastoise with 3 Energy cannot retreat on the opponent's next turn and can retreat again on the turn after. :192-219 checks that both printings behave the same.

claim: Team Rocket's Master Plan confuses the opponent's Active Pokémon unconditionally, then flips a coin; a Tails result also confuses the user's own Active Pokémon.

claim: Red Card forces the opponent to shuffle their entire hand into the deck and draw a new fixed 3-card hand.

claim: Sightseer lets the player look at the top 4 cards of the deck and take exactly 1 into hand.

claim: The Hiking Trail Stadium triggers a draw that refills the player's hand up to 3 cards.

claim: Poke Ball resolves by publicly revealing the found Pokémon (Pumpkaboo) to both players, and the Poke Ball card itself goes to discard after being played.

result.evidence: Half of the claim matches: Poke Ball goes to the discard. apply_action_helpers.rs:990-991 (discard_card_from_hand for any Trainer that is not a Tool or Stadium, run in the prefix before the effect), pinned by s189_hidden_zone_eligibility.rs:87. The 'publicly revealed to both players' half is contradicted. pokemon_search_outcomes (shared_mutations.rs:171-177) moves the card from deck to hand without creating any reveal event; PublicRevealKind has only DeckPrefixThenShuffle (state/mod.rs:231-233). In observation.rs update_knowledge, the opponent's view loses what it knew about the searcher's hand whenever that hand changes (observation.rs:678-683, known.opponent_hand.clear()). So the opposing bot learns only that a card arrived, never that it was Pumpkaboo, until Pumpkaboo is benched. The engine's knowledge tracking therefore hides the fetched Basic from the opponent, which is the opposite of 'revealed to both players'.
result.note: The contradiction is probably with the claim, not an engine bug. Turn 7 of 221914 is the owner's (Dustin's) turn (Pocket Deck Lab .../battle-20260907-221914/REVIEW.md:25, DRAFT_LEDGER.md:14). Dustin's own screen showing his own Pumpkaboo says nothing about what the opponent saw, so 'public' is the reviewer's inference. rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:148-149 records that the opponent's Poke Ball result goes to hand face-down (seen frame by frame, x3) and gives Dustin's general rule that any card moving from deck to hand is hidden. The engine agrees with that. Checking what the opponent sees on that turn would need footage from the opponent's side, or an opponent Poke Ball in Dustin's footage. The T2 entry in the same review ('Poke Ball ... directly reveals Team Rocket's Slowpoke') is on the opponent's turn and is worth a frame check, but its coverage note (COVERAGE.md:39) suggests Slowpoke only became visible when it was benched.

result.evidence: Promotion swaps the whole PlayedCard (apply_action_helpers.rs:957), so the new Active keeps its Energy. engine/tests/trainers/skyla_test.rs:65-122 shows this: the promoted Charmander keeps its Fire and later pays its own retreat with it. Once the retreat finishes, Attach to the new Active (index 0) is offered as usual.

claim: Sabrina's forced switch of the opponent's Active Pokémon is a Supporter effect distinct from a normal retreat: no retreat cost is paid, and the switched Pokémon (e.g., Rattata) keeps its attached Energy.

Activate goes to apply_retreat(..., is_free=true) (apply_action.rs:823-830, 1432-1434), which calls apply_activate straight away (apply_action_helpers.rs:939-966): no cost check, no Energy discarded, has_retreated not set. The switched Pokémon moves with its Energy because the PlayedCard is swapped. Tests: engine/tests/mechanics/retreat_test.rs:39-91 (a forced Activate doesn't use up the turn's retreat) and engine/tests/trainers/skyla_test.rs:65-122 (Energy stays on a Pokémon moved by an Activate switch).

claim: Team Rocket's Goo-zooka (Item) adds +1 to the opposing Active's retreat cost, lasting through the opponent's next turn; seen raising Weezing ex's retreat cost by 1, distinct from attaching a Pokémon Tool.

This is an effect on the Pokémon, not a Tool: the Item is discarded (apply_action_helpers.rs:990-991), unlike Tools, which leave the hand at :988-989. get_retreat_cost adds it after the reductions (hooks/retreat.rs:220-232).
