claim: Lusamine lets the player choose an Ultra Beast in play and attach 2 random Energy from the discard pile to it; this attachment is separate from and in addition to that turn's normal one Energy attachment.

result.evidence: can_play_lusamine (engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:722-747) requires the opponent to have at least 1 point, an Ultra Beast of yours in play, and Energy in your discard. lusamine_effect (apply_trainer_action.rs:2045-2063) lets the player pick the Ultra Beast (AttachFromDiscard). forecast_attach_from_discard (apply_action.rs:1678-1721) picks 2 random Energy from the discard, weighted by count. The attach goes through attach_energy_from_discard (state/energy.rs:55-74), which never touches energy_zone.current, so the turn's Energy Zone attach (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92, cleared only when is_turn_energy is set, energy.rs:26-28) is still available.
result.note: No test covers Lusamine specifically; this rests on the code. The card also needs the opponent to have at least 1 point. The claim leaves that out but doesn't contradict it.

claim: Retreating a Pokémon to the Bench cures its Special Conditions: seen curing Confusion alone, and separately curing both Poison and Confusion at once.

That function clears poisoned, paralyzed, asleep, burned and confused together (engine/src/state/played_card.rs:378-386), so Poison and Confusion are cured at once. Tests: engine/tests/mechanics/confusion_test.rs:92-141 (a Confused Charizard is no longer Confused after retreating) and engine/tests/video_evidence/xatu_checkup.rs:243-262 (a Poisoned Mega Lucario is not Poisoned after retreating).

claim: Energy-attach/recover effects from an Ability, attack, or Item (Roar in Unison, Flame Patch, Lusamine, Elemental Switch) are separate from and stack with the single ordinary per-turn Energy Zone attachment, letting a second Pokémon also gain Energy that turn.

result.evidence: The ordinary attach is Attach with is_turn_energy=true. It is offered only while energy_zone.current is set (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92) and clears it (state/energy.rs:26-28). Roar in Unison maps to AttachEnergyFromZoneToSelfAndDamage{Darkness,2,30} (effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:503-508), which runs attach_energy_from_zone(..., is_turn_energy=false) (apply_abilities_action.rs:695-716), so the turn's Energy is left alone. Flame Patch (apply_trainer_action.rs:2172-2174) and Lusamine (apply_action.rs:1678-1721) attach from the discard (energy.rs:55-74). Elemental Switch uses MoveEnergy (apply_action.rs:1007-1037). Neither touches the Energy Zone. Test: engine/tests/pokemon/kubfu_training_test.rs:20-40 shows an effect's Zone attach does not use up the turn's Energy (energy_zone[0].current is still Some(Fighting)).
result.note: There's no test for Roar in Unison or Flame Patch themselves. They share the same non-turn paths.

claim: The turn's ordinary Energy Zone attachment can supply an attack's Energy requirement immediately, confirmed when Decidueye's Energy rose from 1 to 2 via attachment right before it used Pierce the Pain that same turn.

result.evidence: The turn attach is a free action (move_generation/mod.rs:77-92), and attacks are generated in the same main phase from the Energy currently attached (mod.rs:110-112). The attached Energy counts right away. Test: engine/tests/video_evidence/celebi_energy.rs:222-232 attaches the turn's Energy to Celebi, going from 3 to 4 Energy, and the 4-cost Powerful Bloom is then offered that same turn. claim: Team Rocket Grunt's flip-until-tails Energy discard is capped by the Energy actually attached — it cannot discard more Energy than is present even with additional Heads flips.

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:2511-2540 (team_rocket_grunt_outcomes). The saturation point is set to the number of Energy on the opponent's Active (lines 2514-2516). geometric_until_tails_saturated (engine/src/actions/outcomes.rs:316-325, classes built at outcomes.rs:138-171) puts every run of that many Heads or more into one final branch that uses exactly that many Heads. So 3 Heads against 2 Energy gives the same result as 2 Heads. The mutation also stops early when the Active has no Energy left (lines 2522-2528), so it can never discard more Energy than is attached. The play gate at move_generation_trainer.rs:1009-1023 requires the opponent's Active to have at least one Energy. The real game's behaviour is on record in PocketDeckSim/rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:91 ('3 Heads discarded only the 2 Energy that existed', OBSERVED 220914). The audit note at rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/trainers.md:263 agrees with the code.
result.note: No test pins this cap. I grepped engine/tests and the engine/src test modules and found no Team Rocket Grunt test, so the evidence is the code alone. The claim's source is marked 'inferred', but rules/_research_notes/R2_battle_observations.md:162 quotes battle-20260907-220914-221051 REVIEW.md Turn 8 as DIRECT: 3 Heads then 1 Tails, and Gyarados had only 2 Energy, so both were removed. A suggested regression test: opponent Active with 2 Energy, force a 3H+T flip sequence, and check that exactly 2 are discarded and the Bench is untouched.

claim: A Supporter can switch the user's own Active Pokemon for a Benched one entirely for free, fully bypassing the retreat cost: Sabrina switched to a Benched Mewtwo with no Energy paid.

result.evidence: The claim is right that the switch is free, and the engine matches that. The claim is wrong about WHOSE Pokémon gets switched. The card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:5138, A1 225) says: 'Switch out your opponent's Active Pokémon to the Bench. (Your opponent chooses the new Active Pokémon.)'. The engine does exactly this. sabrina_effect (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:841-854) offers SimpleAction::Activate{player: opponent} and lets the opponent choose. Activate goes to apply_retreat(player, state, idx, is_free=true) (apply_action.rs:823-830). The free branch (apply_action.rs:1431-1435) calls apply_activate (apply_action_helpers.rs:939-966), which only swaps the two Pokémon. It discards no Energy and does not set has_retreated; only finish_paid_retreat at apply_action.rs:1454-1468 does those things. Test: engine/tests/rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:44-55. Player 1 plays Sabrina and player 0's Active becomes the benched Snorlax (line 55). That test does not check Energy, but the code path has no discard.
result.note: The claim's wording does not match its own source. Boss Folder/video-review-coordinator-2026-09-09/previously-finished-audit/battle-234514/REVIEW.md:23 says the OPPONENT played Sabrina on Turn 5, forcing Dustin's Mega Blaziken to the Bench and bringing Castform Active 'without a retreat payment'. Mewtwo was the opponent's benched Pokémon, and it received an attachment right after the switch. Nobody switched 'to a Benched Mewtwo'. That recorded event matches the engine exactly. If the claim is read literally (a Supporter switches the USER'S OWN Active), Sabrina cannot do that in the game or in the engine. Please correct the claim text rather than change the engine.

claim: A Supporter can move already-attached Energy between a player's own Pokémon: the Supporter Psychic moved 1 random Energy from Bench to Active (counts 5→4 and 1→2), immediately affecting that turn's damage scaling.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:78259, B4 150 / B4 190): the player can use it only if their Active has the Psychic attack. It says to choose 1 of the opponent's Benched Pokémon and move a random Energy from it to the opponent's Active. So the Energy stays on one side of the board, but it is the OPPONENT's side. The source (Boss Folder/.../review-intake-61-2026-09-09/RESEARCH_HANDOFF.md:7) agrees: the opponent's Numel went 5→4 and the opponent's Moltres went 1→2, which raised Indeedee's damage. Engine: psychic_effect (apply_trainer_action.rs:2134-2145) lets the player who played the card pick a Bench source from psychic_energy_sources (card_logic/psychic.rs:18-27, opponent's Benched Pokémon with Energy). MoveRandomOpponentEnergyToActive (apply_action.rs:928-933) moves exactly 1 Energy from that Pokémon to the opponent's Active, so the counts go down 1 and up 1. Test: engine/tests/trainers/psychic_test.rs:17-69 checks that the player who played the card chooses (line 46), that only a Bench Pokémon with Energy is offered (47-57), and that Energy goes Bench 2→1 and Active 0→1 (61-68). The damage change on the same turn: Indeedee ex's Psychic (B1 121, 30 + 30 per opponent Active Energy) maps to ExtraDamagePerEnergy{opponent:true} (effect_mechanic_map.rs:2205-2208). extra_damage_per_energy (apply_attack_action.rs:4363-4380) reads the defender's Energy at the moment of the attack, so a move made earlier that turn counts right away. 30+30×1=60 before the move and 30+30×2=90 after, consistent with the 90/120/180 values seen for 2/3/5 Energy.
result.note: The claim's phrase 'between a player's own Pokémon' is only correct if 'player' means the OPPONENT. The Supporter moves the opponent's Energy from their Bench to their Active, not the user's. Separately, the engine differs from the card in a way that does not change these counts. apply_action.rs:930-932 moves the source's LAST attached Energy, not a random one ('Using the last energy instead of a random one to avoid expanding the game tree'). That only matters when the Benched Pokémon holds mixed Energy types and the type later matters (for example, a type-specific cost or count). It does not matter for a count-based attack like Indeedee's. rules/_research_notes/audit_2026-09-22/trainers.md:207 says this card 'is correctly random', which is stale or wrong compared with the current code. No test pins the Supporter-then-attack damage sequence end to end; the scaling is shown from code.

claim: Knocking out a non-ex Pokémon awards 1 point, an ex Pokémon 2 points, and a Mega ex Pokémon 3 points; reaching 3 total points ends the match immediately as a Victory, confirmed across many separate battles (single ex/Mega-ex KOs alone can reach the win).

result.evidence: Point values: engine/src/models/card.rs:204-216. Immediate end: engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:845-855 sets winner = Win(p) as soon as points[p] >= 3 after the KO wave, and returns before any promotion is queued (:874-886). Pinned by engine/tests/terminal_win_policy_test.rs:56-66 (a single Mega Mawile ex KO from 2 points -> winner Win(0)) and engine/tests/boiler_smog_public_forecast_test.rs:325.
result.note: The engine has one narrow exception, apply_action_helpers.rs:832-842 (rules4 T2): if the player reaching 3 loses their own last Pokémon in the same exchange while the opponent still has Pokémon and fewer than 3 points, the result is a Tie. Both players reaching 3 together is also a Tie (:845-848). Neither case contradicts the recorded wins.

claim: On a Knockout, the sequence is fixed: attack damage resolves, the Pokémon is Knocked Out and discarded, point(s) are awarded to the opponent immediately, then its owner promotes a new Active from the Bench, even if it is their sole remaining Pokémon.

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/attack_outcome.rs:139-209: damage, then attack effects, then retaliation, then handle_knockouts. In engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:652-886, the KO wave runs on_knockout hooks (700-709), then award_points (733), then discard_from_play (795), then the win check (845-868), then trigger_promotion_or_declare_winner (880-886). That call queues a Promote frame even when only one Benched Pokémon exists (engine/src/state/mod.rs:1381-1398). Pinned by engine/tests/tools/raikou_rocky_helmet_order_test.rs:49-67 (Active empty, points [0,2], then a Promote choice for the sole Benched Bulbasaur) and engine/tests/tools/tools_integration_test.rs:209-228 (KO -> +1 point -> opponent prompted to Promote their only Benched Squirtle).
result.note: One exact-ordering detail: inside the engine's single atomic KO step, points are awarded (line 733) before the card is discarded (line 795). The claim says discard, then points. No player choice or other effect can happen between the two, so the order cannot be observed and has no effect. The observable order (damage -> KO -> points -> promotion) matches. Promotion is skipped when the award reaches 3 (the game is already over), and the engine shows a one-option Promote choice rather than filling the spot automatically.

claim: When a KO triggers both a held Tool's retaliation and a separate on-KO ability, already-triggered damage effects keep resolving after the Pokémon hits 0 HP: Rocky Helmet's retaliation damage lands first, then Destiny Burst's damage also lands on the already-KO'd attacker.

result.evidence: Rocky Helmet: handle_attack_retaliation (engine/src/actions/attack_outcome.rs:197, or engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:557 when deferred) runs before handle_knockouts (attack_outcome.rs:208 / apply_action.rs:560), with the KO'd holder still in play at 0 HP. Destiny Burst: on_knockout runs for the whole wave while every member is still in play (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:696-709). It deals 70 to the attacker via handle_damage_only even at 0 HP (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:2185-2230; mapping in engine/src/actions/effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:195-201). Pinned by engine/tests/pokemon/team_rocket_electrode_destiny_burst_test.rs:8-63 (Castform KO'd by Rocky Helmet, then Destiny Burst still resolves; points [1,1]; both seats).
result.note: The test pins that the sequence resolves without error and scores both KOs. It cannot show the 70 numerically because the attacker is already at 0 HP. rules/02_damage_knockouts_points.md:98 records the same observed order (Helmet 20 -> Destiny Burst 70 -> KOs, points, promotion).

result.evidence: The Glimmora text 'When this Pokémon is Knocked Out, flip a coin. claim: The on-screen point track shows at most 3 circles and never displays a running total above 3, even when actual cumulative or single-KO point awards exceed 3 (e.g. Mega ex +3, or sums like 1+2+2=4 shown capped as 3-1), undercounting real points earned.

It stores and exports the raw total: engine/src/state/mod.rs:1212-1215 (award_points adds with no clamp) and engine/src/game_result_exporter.rs:307 (final_points: state.points). engine/tests/terminal_win_policy_test.rs:64 asserts points [5,2] after a Mega ex KO from 2.

result.evidence: engine/src/state/mod.rs:1212-1215 award_points does points[player] += amount with no cap at 3. engine/tests/terminal_win_policy_test.rs:56-66 pins an overflow (points [5,2] after a +3 Mega ex KO from 2). For this recording, a Zapdos ex KO (+2 via card.rs:211-212) from 2 points leaves the engine at 4, not 3, and game_result_exporter.rs:307 would export 4.

The claim rests on one on-screen reading. R181 and rules/01_game_structure.md:89 treat that same 3-circle track as a display cap, so the video likely cannot tell a real cap from a display cap. The in-game internal total cannot be observed.

Move generation is at engine/src/move_generation/move_generation_trainer.rs:663-685: not on the user's first turn (turn_count<=2), not under Malamar's Jammer, and a valid Basic-in-play/Stage-2-in-hand pair must exist. apply_trainer_action.rs:1905-1928 offers Evolve{from_deck:false} for each pair, and apply_action.rs:818-822 routes it to apply_evolve. The engine data has every line in the claim: Kingambit<-Bisharp<-Pawniard, Corviknight ex<-Corvisquire<-Rookidee (database.rs:66845), Gardevoir B2 065<-Kirlia<-Ralts, Stoutland<-Herdier<-Lillipup (48436), Aegislash<-Doublade<-Honedge (47733), Crobat<-Golbat<-Zubat (66286), Hisuian Goodra<-Hisuian Sliggoo<-Goomy (72711). Mega Blaziken ex is stage 2 from Combusken (database.rs:44559), so Torchic->Mega Blaziken ex is in the table. Pinning tests: rare_candy.rs:193-201 (Bulbasaur->Venusaur allowed), 203-211 (Ivysaur refused), 213-221 (wrong line refused), 223-231 (fossil to Rampardos).

claim: A Mega Pokémon ex can evolve directly from a Basic Pokémon with no intermediate stage, via its own printed 'Evolves from' line or via Rare Candy, skipping the Stage 1 form entirely; confirmed for Electrike→Mega Manectric ex and Riolu→Mega Lucario ex.

result.evidence: The engine data prints both Megas as Stage 1 evolving straight from the Basic: Mega Manectric ex is stage 1 from Electrike (engine/src/database.rs:62082-62087), and Mega Lucario ex is stage 1 from Riolu (database.rs:65847). So a normal hand evolution is generated for them (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:195-219, using Card::can_evolve_into name match at models/card.rs:269-272), with no intermediate card. The Rare Candy route exists only for Stage 2 Megas such as Mega Blaziken ex (stage 2 from Combusken, database.rs:44559; rare_candy.rs:75-87). The engine refuses Rare Candy onto a Stage 1 Mega (rare_candy.rs:97), which matches the printed Rare Candy text.
result.note: The phrase 'skipping the Stage 1 form' is a misreading for these two cards. Mega Manectric ex and Mega Lucario ex are themselves the Stage 1, so nothing is skipped. The support shows no Rare Candy: the 232617 review, REVIEW.md line 75, says 'no Rare Candy or separate Lucario play occurs'. The claim's 'or via Rare Candy' is right only for Stage 2 Megas (Mega Blaziken ex, Mega Gardevoir ex), which R183 covers.

claim: A player may evolve more than one Pokémon in the same turn; the owner evolved both a Benched Varoom and the Active Varoom into Revavroom within a single turn.

result.evidence: engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:195-219 offers an Evolve for every in-play Pokémon that meets these conditions: not first turn, not played_this_turn, and can_evolve_into. There is no per-turn evolution counter. apply_evolve (apply_action.rs:1511, to_playable_card(to_card, true)) marks only the evolved Pokémon played_this_turn, so the limit is one evolution per Pokémon, not one per turn. So a Benched Varoom and the Active Varoom can each become Revavroom in the same turn. The unit test apply_action.rs:1848-1901 (test_apply_evolve) evolves the Active Mankey and then a Benched Mankey into Primeape in the same state, with no turn change, and both succeed. engine/examples/legality_scan.rs:139-146 flags a 'second evolution this turn' only for the same Pokémon.
result.note: No test in engine/tests evolves two different Pokémon in one turn through generate_possible_actions. The evidence is the move-generation code plus the apply_evolve unit test. rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:39 agrees: 'As many evolutions per turn as you like'.

claim: Evolving preserves a Pokémon's existing state rather than resetting it: damage carries onto the new stage's higher max HP (e.g., Revavroom 100/120, Exeggutor ex 150/160, Electrode 20/70), and attached Energy and Tools stay attached (e.g., 2 Fighting Energy on Mega Lucario ex; Sitrus Berry, Rocky Helmet).

result.evidence: engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1503-1531 (apply_evolve) builds a new PlayedCard for the evolution, then copies the old damage counters (1521-1522), attached_energy (1523), attached_tools (1524) and cards_behind (1525-1526), and calls refresh_hp_bonuses_all (1528). Remaining HP is therefore the new max HP minus the same damage: 20 damage on Varoom gives 100/120 Revavroom, and 10 on Exeggcute gives 150/160 Exeggutor ex. Fossils go through the same path (Old Amber -> Aerodactyl ex; get_stage treats a fossil as Basic, hooks/core.rs:105-117). Pinning tests: apply_action.rs:1848-1901 test_apply_evolve (30 damage and the Energy carried, with the new 90 max HP); engine/tests/rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:72-74 (Rattata at 10 HP becomes Raticate at 50 HP, damage carried through the Game API).
result.note: No test pins Tools staying attached on evolution. That part rests on the code line apply_action.rs:1524. A Tool whose HP bonus depends on stage (Elegant Cape) is recomputed after evolving (played_card.rs:299-301), which matches the observed Type: Null -> Silvally case.

claim: The item Quick-Grow Extract evolves a Pokemon (Metapod into Butterfree) outside the normal turn-based evolution restriction, and its existing 70 damage carries over unchanged to the new form.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/card.py): Quick-Grow Extract evolves a chosen Grass Pokémon into a random Grass Pokémon from the deck that evolves from it. It prints two limits: not on your first turn, and not on a Pokémon put into play this turn. The engine enforces the same two limits (move_generation_trainer.rs:968-988; apply_trainer_action.rs:2412-2433, which offers a ChooseRandomEvolutionTarget for each non-played_this_turn Grass Pokémon). random_typed_evolution_outcomes (apply_trainer_action.rs:2462-2509) then calls apply_evolve(..., from_deck=true) at :2502, which carries damage (apply_action.rs:1521-1522). Metapod B3b 002 (80 HP) with 70 damage becomes Butterfree B3b 003 (130 HP, stage 2 from Metapod, database.rs:71682) at 60/130, as recorded. On turn 4 the game is past turn_count<=2 (state/mod.rs:1227-1229), and Metapod had been in play since turn 1. Test: engine/tests/rules_repair_trainers.rs:235-273 (the player picks the target, then the target evolves from the deck). Damage carry-over is pinned by apply_action.rs:1848-1901.
result.note: The phrase 'outside the normal turn-based evolution restriction' is not supported. Quick-Grow Extract prints the normal limits and the engine keeps them (rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:41-42). In the recorded case (150630, turn 4) Metapod had evolved from Caterpie by Quick Growth at the end of turn 1, so no exception was exercised. If the phrase meant that Quick-Grow Extract can hit a Pokémon put into play or evolved this turn, the engine refuses that (played_this_turn filter at apply_trainer_action.rs:2418). The recording does not show it.

claim: Evolving a Pokémon affected by a Special Condition cures it, confirmed for Confused (Charmeleon, Salazzle) and Asleep (Bulbasaur→Ivysaur), across 3 evolving Pokémon in 2 separate battles.

result.evidence: apply_evolve (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1510-1511) builds a new PlayedCard with to_playable_card. PlayedCard::new (engine/src/state/played_card.rs:84-117) starts poisoned, paralyzed, asleep, burned and confused all false, so every Special Condition ends. Move generation has no status check for evolving (move_generation/mod.rs:195-219), so a Confused or Asleep Active can still evolve. Quick-Grow Extract (the Bulbasaur->Ivysaur case in 190031) uses the same apply_evolve (apply_trainer_action.rs:2502). Pinning tests: engine/tests/status_action_restriction_test.rs:198-212 (Asleep Eevee evolves into Espeon and is no longer Asleep); engine/tests/paralysis_lifecycle_test.rs:283-304 (Paralysis cleared by evolving); engine/tests/rules_repair_timing.rs:294-312 (Poison cleared when Caterpie evolves).
result.note: No test pins Confused specifically. It is cleared by the same new-PlayedCard path as the others.

claim: Primeval Law blocks playing a card from hand to evolve the Active Pokémon while its owner Aerodactyl ex is in play, shown as a passive, continuously-displayed Ability notice rather than a one-off failed-attempt message.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/card.py, Aerodactyl ex A1a 046): 'Your opponent can't play any Pokémon from their hand to evolve their Active Pokémon.' The text does not require Aerodactyl ex itself to be Active. The engine: can_evolve_at_position (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:252-258) refuses hand evolution at position 0 whenever has_opponent_aerodactyl_ex_primeval_law (:270-282) finds any opponent Pokémon in play with PreventOpponentActiveEvolution, whether it is Active or Benched. Tests: mod.rs:373-408 (the Active evolution is blocked), mod.rs:410-450 (Bench evolution is not blocked), engine/tests/pokemon/legacy_ability_logic_test.rs:161-177 (no Evolve at in_play_idx 0 through the Game API).
result.note: The blocking rule matches. The part about the game showing a lasting on-screen notice is UI only; the engine has no display, so that part is not covered. Separate gap found while checking: Rare Candy does not respect Primeval Law. can_play_rare_candy (move_generation_trainer.rs:663-685) checks only Malamar's Jammer, and rare_candy_effect (apply_trainer_action.rs:1905-1928) offers the Active Basic as a target. Under Primeval Law the engine would let Rare Candy put a Stage 2 from hand onto the Active, which the printed text seems to forbid. The recordings don't test this.

claim: Evolving a Pokémon clears a pending applied effect on it: Teary Attack's '-30 damage next opponent turn' on Exeggcute was cleared by evolving into Exeggutor ex before that turn, so the following Tropical Swing hit for its full 80.

result.evidence: Teary Attack (Bonsly B3 078) is mapped as DamageAndCardEffect{opponent:true, ReducedAttackDamage{30}, duration:1} (engine/src/actions/effect_mechanic_map.rs:507-515). That effect is stored on the Defending Pokémon's PlayedCard and subtracted from its attacks at hooks/core.rs:1862-1875. apply_evolve creates a new PlayedCard with an empty effects list (apply_action.rs:1511; played_card.rs:113) and does not copy effects (apply_action.rs:1521-1526). So once Exeggcute evolves, Exeggutor ex's Tropical Swing that same turn has no -30: 40, plus 40 on heads, for the full 80. Test: engine/tests/rules_repair_attacker_debuff.rs:63-78 (recorded_rattata_evolution_clears_teary_attack_and_bite_scores). In that test Bonsly's Teary Attack hits Rattata, Rattata evolves into Raticate on its owner's turn, and the next attack KOs Bonsly with no reduction. It is the same code path as the 235356 Exeggcute case.
result.note: On timing: the evolution and the Tropical Swing both happen during the debuffed player's own turn (the 'opponent's next turn' from Bonsly's side). The engine clears the effect at the moment of evolving, so any attack after that in the same turn is unreduced. 'Full 80' needs heads on Tropical Swing's coin; the engine does 40 on tails. rules/10_review_of_rules1_2026-09-22.md:55-58 cites both recordings, 224540 and 235356.

claim: Regigigas's 'Seal of Antiquity' ability/effect prevents it from using any attack at all for as long as it remains Active; it never attacked across the entire recorded game.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:67858-67859, B3 134): 'If you don't have Regirock, Regice, and Registeel on your Bench, this Pokémon can't attack.' The mapping is at engine/src/actions/effect_ability_mechanic_map.rs:782-787 (CannotAttackWithoutBenchedNames). engine/src/move_generation/attacks.rs:36-40 returns no attacks while the check at attacks.rs:155-174 finds a missing Regi. Tests: engine/tests/pokemon/regigigas_seal_of_antiquity_test.rs:62-88 (any missing Regi means no attack) and :48-58 (all three Regis on the Bench allow Giga Turbo). In 181914 (Boss Folder battle-20260907-181914/REVIEW.md rows T2-T7), Regigigas was Active from T2 with no Regi on the Bench and was KO'd on T7. Alolan Muk only arrived on T8, so the engine would also offer it no attack for its whole stay.
result.note: The claim is broader than the card and the engine. The seal is conditional: the engine lifts it when Regirock, Regice and Registeel are all on the owner's Bench, or when Abilities are switched off. The tests show Alolan Muk unsealing it (:137-173) and Prickly Powder unsealing it (:214-224). Alolan Muk is in Dustin's own deck 01 (decks/dustin/01-muk-glimmora-kingambit-regigigas.txt), so 'never at all' would be wrong in a game where Muk is in play while Regigigas is Active. This game also does not isolate the Seal. Regigigas never got any Energy (the Darkness went to Glimmet T2, Pawniard T4 and Kingambit T6), so it could not have paid Giga Turbo's CCC anyway.

claim: Baxcalibur's Ice Maker ability generates 1 Water Energy attachable to any one of the user's own Pokémon, usable once per turn per Baxcalibur in play; two Baxcalibur copies in play each triggered Ice Maker independently the same turn, each attaching its own Energy.

result.evidence: Card text (lib/deckgym-database.json:60092, B2a 036): '...attach it to the [W] Pokémon in the Active Spot.' The engine follows this text. move_generation_abilities.rs:112-114 and 361-371 offer Ice Maker only when the Active Pokémon is [W]. apply_abilities_action.rs:662-666 always attaches to in_play_idx 0, the Active. claim: A defending Pokémon's Securely Sheltered ability flips a coin on each incoming damaging attack: Tails lets the attack's full displayed damage through (70, then 110 twice), while Heads fully prevents the attack for 0 damage.

Per attack, a coin is flipped only if the Pokémon would take more than 0 damage. Tails lets the full damage through; heads subtracts 80, floored at 0 (apply_attack_action.rs:178-216; attack_outcome.rs:547-603, saturating_sub at :589). Pinned by tests/pokemon/hisuian_goodra_securely_sheltered_test.rs:16 (120 damage: tails 120, heads 40) and :64 (10 damage: heads 0, and the Poison still lands). In this battle the one Heads was against a 70-damage Quick Straight, which gave 0 (rules/02_damage_knockouts_points.md:31; rules/_research_notes/R2_battle_observations.md:104). The engine also gives 0 there, and it matches the tails results of 70, 110 and 110.

Side finding on ordering, not visible in this battle: the engine subtracts the 80 from the attack's printed damage (attack_outcome.rs:589). modify_damage adds attacker bonuses such as Fighting Coach and Weakness only afterwards (hooks/core.rs:1854-1885). rules/02:29 puts this reduction at step 4, after Weakness. Here both orders give 0: printed 50 minus 80 drops the hit, so Coach's +20 is never added, and the game's 70 minus 80 is also 0. The results differ when printed damage is under 80 but printed plus bonuses is over 80. Example: 70 printed + 20 Coach gives 10 in the game and 0 in the engine. They also differ under ×2 Weakness.

claim: During Pokémon Checkup, Poison damage resolves before other Checkup sub-effects (e.g. the Burn coin-flip check), and a Pokémon already Knocked Out receives no further Checkup effects such as Burn damage or its coin flip.

result.evidence: First half matches: apply_pokemon_checkup (apply_action_helpers.rs:286-335) runs, per player with the turn player first, Poison (296-300), then Burn 20 and its coin (301-309), then Sleep (310-316), then Paralysis. After both players come Snowy Terrain/Sand Slammer (324) and Blessed Salt (325). Second half contradicts when read as 'KO'd by Poison inside the Checkup'. The engine does not KO anything until handle_knockouts at line 326, after all Checkup effects. The Burn targets are collected before any damage (lines 122/151), so a Pokémon that Poison took to 0 still takes Burn's 20 (handle_damage_only, clamped at 0 per line 570) and still gets its Burn coin as forecast branches (lines 127-128). Snowy Terrain and Blessed Salt still apply to it too. Blessed Salt can therefore rescue it: engine/tests/rules_repair_timing.rs:46-63 (checkup_heals_before_knockout_in_both_seats) pins a Poisoned 10-HP Bulbasaur with Garganacl surviving at 10 HP with points [0,0]. The claim implies it would be KO'd with no further effects. That heal rescue is the only divergence that changes play: Burn damage and the Burn coin on a 0-HP Pokémon leave the engine state unchanged. Read as 'KO'd before the Checkup' (225430: Electrode KO'd by the attack), the engine matches: attack KOs are handled inside the attack, and collect_checkup_targets (254-284) only sees Pokémon still in play.
result.note: The contradiction probably comes from a claim error, not an engine bug. The claim's own source, the accepted 004344 REVIEW.md Turn 6, records 'Burn check results in Tails (03:22.400)'. That is after Poison KO'd Hypno at 03:18.000 and before the discard at 03:23.400, and the OCR has 'Pokémon Checkup — Burned' at 201-202 s. So the real game flipped Burn for a 0-HP Pokémon, as the engine does and as the official Tips say ('no HP remaining at the end of Pokémon Checkup is Knocked Out', rules/03 §5.4). The 010316 support only shows Poison before Blessed Salt in non-lethal cases. A lethal heal rescue is still unobserved (05 #4, 08 T3). A recording of 08 T3 would settle the heal-rescue point.

result.evidence: Ilima (A3 149/A3 191) queues SimpleAction::ReturnPokemonToHand for each damaged [C] target (engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:1836-1846; targets from engine/src/card_logic/ilima.rs:3-11, and the Active slot 0 is included). The handler, engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:1173-1188 (apply_return_pokemon_to_hand), takes the PlayedCard out of play and puts only the Pokémon card and its evolution chain (cards_behind) into hand (1177-1179). It sends attached_tools to discard_piles (1180) and attached_energy to discard_energies (1181), then refreshes HP bonuses. Because the slot is 0 here, it then triggers promotion or declares a winner (1185-1187). Nothing attached goes back to hand. The pinning test is engine/tests/revavroom_tools_test.rs:466-501 (return_and_shuffle_actions_conserve_tools_and_energy). It returns a Pokémon carrying Giant Cape, Rocky Helmet and 1 Metal Energy with ReturnPokemonToHand and asserts both tools are in discard_piles and the energy is in discard_energies (lines 492-494).

For the Active, the same function runs and only the promotion step is added. engine/tests/trainers/ilima_test.rs:61-108 tests Ilima on the Active, but it only checks that the card reaches hand and that promotion is offered, not where attachments go. Elegant Cape (B3b 065) is a normal tool in the engine (engine/src/state/played_card.rs:300), so it goes through attached_tools like any other tool. The rules docs agree: rules/04_actions_cards_effects.md:98 says the Tool goes to discard, never to hand, [COMMUNITY]+[OBSERVED].

claim: The post-game results screen's 'Damage done' stat only counts the player's own attack damage dealt, excluding damage the opponent inflicted on itself (e.g., Hydreigon's self-damage was not counted).

result.evidence: The engine has no post-game results screen and no per-player 'Damage done' statistic. Its only stats collectors are engine/src/simulation_event_handler.rs:218-247 (ComputedStats/StatsCollector: durations, turns, plies, wins, ties) and engine/src/gameplay_stats_collector.rs:12-60 (AggregatedStats: game length, empty-deck turn, hand sizes, first-seen cards, first-used attacks). Neither tracks damage dealt, so it can't count Hydreigon's Roar in Unison self-damage (B1 Hydreigon: 'do 30 damage to this Pokémon') either way. This is a UI-only fact about the game client and has no effect on simulated games.
result.note: Only the game client's results screen could settle this. The support is a single 'seen' observation, and it has no effect on game rules.

claim: On Turn 1, the player going first cannot generate or attach Energy and cannot attack; confirmed directly (not just inferred) across multiple recorded battles.

result.evidence: Energy part is pinned by tests. The turn-1 start sets turn_count=1 with no energy rotation (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:72-76, comment 'no energy generation'). Setup only pre-fills `next` (engine/src/state/mod.rs:768-772). The first rotation happens in advance_turn (state/mod.rs:1207, 931-932). Attach is offered only when energy_zone.current is Some (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:77-92). Tests: engine/tests/engine/apply_actions_test.rs:228-249 (test_energy_zone_state_at_start_of_turn_1 asserts the first player's current is None on turn 1) and apply_actions_test.rs:202-206 (no Attach actions right after initialization). Attack part: the engine has no turn-1 attack ban. generate_attack_actions gates only on cost (engine/src/move_generation/attacks.rs:70-76). With 0 energy, Chien-Pao ex (B2a 037, lib/deckgym-database.json:60111-60128; cheapest attack Icicle costs [W]) gets no attack offered on Turn 1, which matches the recordings.
result.note: The recordings are consistent with the engine, but the blanket 'cannot attack' goes too far. The engine offers a 0-cost attack on Turn 1: attacks.rs has no turn check, and the comment 'only starting on turn 2' at move_generation/mod.rs:110 is stale. RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md:38-41 and the official FAQ say this is correct. Card-effect Zone attachments on the first turn also still happen, e.g. Zeraora's Thunderclap Flash at the end of turn 1/2 (engine/src/hooks/core.rs:521-551). The claim should be narrowed to 'no Energy Zone energy on Turn 1, so no attack with an Energy cost'. Do not change the engine to ban all Turn-1 attacks. No test checks that a 0-cost attack is offered on turn 1. bonsly_teary_attack_test.rs:10-33 applies Teary Attack on turn 1 directly but never asserts it is legal.

Playing any Supporter sets has_played_support=true (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:993-995). It resets only at end-of-turn maintenance (engine/src/state/mod.rs:952). result.note: The claim's evidence is inferred only: no double-Supporter turn seen across one 19-turn match. That is weak evidence on its own, but the engine agrees and so does the official one-Supporter-per-turn rule (RULES_FOR_AGENTS.md:45).

claim: The game warns at end of turn (or when confirming an attack) if a Supporter card was left unplayed or a generated Energy unattached, but does not force the action — turns can end or attacks be confirmed regardless.

result.evidence: Nothing is forced: EndTurn is added unconditionally to every free-play action list ('User can always end turn', engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:68-70). generate_attack_actions (engine/src/move_generation/attacks.rs:14-80) does not check whether the turn's Zone energy was attached or a Supporter played; it checks only status, effects and cost. Unused Zone energy is not carried over. energy_zone.current is cleared only on a turn-energy attach (engine/src/state/energy.rs:26-28), and on that player's next turn it is overwritten by rotate_energy_zone (engine/src/state/mod.rs:931-932, called from advance_turn at 1207). There is no dedicated test that EndTurn is offered while Zone energy is unattached and a Supporter is in hand. apply_actions_test.rs:86-99 and 253-280 apply EndTurn on turn 1 directly.
result.note: The on-screen warning itself is UI-only. The engine has no warning concept, so that part is not modeled (nor does it need to be). The gameplay part of the claim, that you can end the turn or attack without playing the Supporter or attaching the energy, matches.

claim: After a retreat, the newly-Active Pokémon is promoted before that turn's ordinary Energy Zone attachment step occurs.

result.evidence: A paid retreat swaps immediately. SimpleAction::Retreat → apply_retreat (engine/src/actions/apply_action.rs:831, 1431-1452) → finish_paid_retreat (1454-1468) → apply_activate, which does in_play_pokemon.swap(0, bench_idx) and marks the new Active moved_to_active_this_turn (engine/src/actions/apply_action_helpers.rs:957, 963-965). It pauses only for a ChooseRetreatEnergy stack choice when several payments are possible. Retreat does not touch energy_zone.current, so on the next free-play step Attach{is_turn_energy:true} is offered for index 0, the new Active (engine/src/move_generation/mod.rs:77-92; energy.rs:76-85 only blocks index 0 under NoEnergyFromZoneToActive). In the cited battle 222326, Hitmonchan's cost drops to 0 via X Speed (implemented, engine/src/actions/apply_trainer_action.rs:98), it retreats, and Aerodactyl ex (A1a 046) becomes Active. The engine can then attach the turn's Fighting to it, which is the recorded sequence.
result.note: The engine has no fixed 'attachment step'. Attach and retreat are both free actions in any order the player chooses, so the observation (retreat, then attach to the new Active) is one legal order, not a forced one. No test pins retreat-then-turn-attach specifically. The closest is engine/tests/video_evidence/flygon_marshadow.rs:224-238 from the same recording, which pins a turn-energy attach to a newly promoted Active after a KO promotion, not a retreat.

claim: Attempting to draw from an empty deck shows a warning message but does not end the battle; play continues normally, observed on 2 separate turns.

result.evidence: C:\Users\dacz8\Projects\Pocket Deck Sim\PocketDeckSim\engine\src\state\mod.rs:811-831. maybe_draw_card calls Deck::draw (engine\src\deck.rs:120-126, which returns None on an empty deck) and on None only writes a debug log, 'cannot draw a card, deck is empty' (mod.rs:829). The start-of-turn draw is queued by advance_turn (mod.rs:1206 -> queue_draw_action 1108-1111) and applied at engine\src\actions\apply_action.rs:778-782, which just loops maybe_draw_card. Nothing on that path touches the winner. The only places the real game sets `winner` are knockout/no-Pokemon resolution (engine\src\actions\apply_action_helpers.rs:840-866, engine\src\state\mod.rs:1388) and the turn-30 tie (mod.rs:1201-1203). result.note: The on-screen warning is UI. The engine only has the debug log, which is not a rules difference. No test pins this directly: grepping engine/tests found no case that empties a deck, runs the turn draw and asserts winner is None. The nearest test is state/mod.rs:1677-1691 (the hand-full draw is a no-op). claim: If a player has no Pokémon left in play (e.g., Knocked Out with no Bench left to promote), the battle ends immediately at the current point total rather than continuing, even below the normal 3-point win total (score seen at 1-2).

result.evidence: C:\Users\dacz8\Projects\Pocket Deck Sim\PocketDeckSim\engine\src\actions\apply_action_helpers.rs:857-868. After every knockout wave and after the 3-point checks, the engine applies the comment 'If a player has no Pokemon left in play, they immediately lose (even if points < 3)': p0_remaining==0 gives Win(1) and p1_remaining==0 gives Win(0), then it returns before any promotion. The Active-KO promotion path does the same through state\mod.rs:1385-1389 (empty Bench -> Win(opponent)). game.rs:185 then stops the loop, so no further turns happen. Tests that pin it: engine\tests\public_reply_verifier_test.rs:151-161 (last Pokemon KO'd by fixed damage; result.winner==Win(actor) with result.points[actor]==1, described as the 'no-Pokemon terminal route before three points'); engine\src\game.rs:545-553 test_ko_by_posion (a Checkup Poison KO of a Bench-less Active ends the game at points 0-1, Win(1), turn_count still 4); engine\tests\trainers\ilima_test.rs:22-57 (the last Pokemon removed by a Trainer means an immediate loss).
result.note: Engine exceptions that do not arise in the 1-2 case seen. If both players are left with no Pokemon, the result is a Tie (apply_action_helpers.rs:858-861). If the side losing its last Pokemon took its own 3rd point in the same exchange, the rules4 T2 rule makes it a Tie (lines 832-842). The ordering is: T2 tie check, then 3-point checks (845-855), then no-Pokemon checks (857-868). With both scores below 3, only the no-Pokemon branch fires, which matches the claim.

claim: Reaching the match's winning point total ends the battle immediately at the moment the qualifying Knockout is scored, even if the losing side still has unpromoted Benched Pokémon or would otherwise have further turns.

result.evidence: C:\Users\dacz8\Projects\Pocket Deck Sim\PocketDeckSim\engine\src\actions\apply_action_helpers.rs:828-855. Once the KO wave's points are awarded (lines 711-760), the engine sets winner=Win(p) when exactly one player has >=3 points and returns. That happens before the promotion loop at lines 870-886 (the comment reads 'short-circuit promotion logic'), so the losing side is never asked to promote a Benched Pokemon, and game.rs:185 ends play with no further turns. The video-bound test engine\tests\video_evidence\flygon_marshadow.rs:240-260 (recording 20260907_222326) pins it: after Marshadow's Revenge KO the losing Active slot is empty, Dartrix survives on the Bench at 80 HP, points [2,3], winner Win(1), and no Promote{player:0} frame is on the stack ('three points must end the game without asking the recorder to promote Dartrix'). A control test also pins it: engine\tests\rules4_t2_simultaneous_finish.rs:47-55 (the opponent keeps two Benched Pokemon and the 3rd point gives Win(actor)).
result.note: Ordering detail: 'the moment the KO is scored' in the engine means after the attack's own effects resolve and handle_knockouts runs (apply_action.rs:770). Before the win is declared, the whole simultaneous KO wave, any nested on-KO retaliation pass (apply_action_helpers.rs:815-826) and any pending point-denial coin (lines 682-694) resolve first. If that leaves both players at >=3, the result is a Tie (lines 845-848). None of this contradicts the claim. It only sharpens what 'immediately' means.
